# PDFix Missing Features — Master Gap List

This consolidates the useful missing-feature ideas discussed for PDFix. It is a planning list, not a claim that these features are implemented. The goal is a simple document workspace with useful PDF, document, photo, and engineering drawing tools—not a copy of every professional publishing suite.

## Status note

The Drive project documents working PDF reading, page organization, crop/resize, markups, supported forms and visual signatures, OCR, image-to-PDF, comparison, and local recovery. The README and architecture describe page-range selection and automatic splitting as implemented, while the older feature tracker still lists automatic splitting as future work. Confirm that tracker status against the current build.

## 1. PDF security, cleanup, and protection

- **Verified permanent redaction:** remove selected text, regions, image content, and underlying objects so hidden information cannot be recovered. Search repeated words/numbers, show every match, and require review before applying.
- **Sanitize before sharing:** inspect and selectively remove metadata, embedded attachments, hidden layers, comments, form values, scripts/actions, and other hidden content. Show what will be removed.
- **Password protection and changes:** add or change PDF passwords using a reviewed implementation; explain permissions and never bypass access controls.
- **Digital signature validation:** detect certificate signatures and report valid, invalid, or unable to verify only when a reviewed validator supports the result. Warn when edits may invalidate signatures.
- **Separate signature types:** distinguish visual signatures, certificate-based signatures, and external signature requests.
- **Safe links and attachments:** show external destinations before opening; list attachments with type/size details and save only to a chosen location. Never execute PDF scripts or auto-open extracted files.
- **Plain-language security report:** explain encryption, signatures, active content, attachments, and unsupported structures.

## 2. Compression, conversion, and PDF creation

- **Compression with quality preview:** show expected size savings and let users inspect quality before saving. Disclose possible loss of text, forms, links, annotations, or other structures.
- **Broader conversions:** support more tested conversions between PDFs, documents, images, and data files. For each, disclose what happens to fonts, page breaks, images, links, bookmarks, forms, and annotations.
- **Multiple images to PDF:** add an ordered image list, per-image rotation, page layout, paper size, and recoverable source references. Current documented workflow makes one PDF from one image.
- **Create PDFs from text/documents:** provide page size, margins, fonts, page breaks, and preview.
- **More export options:** save a page or selected pages as images; export selected pages as separate PDFs; consider reverse PDF-to-image conversion.
- **Page additions:** insert blank pages, replace pages with corrected scans, and add page numbers, headers, footers, watermarks, or reusable Draft/Approved/Reviewed stamps.
- **Metadata tools:** inspect and optionally edit or remove title, author, subject, keywords, and other supported metadata.
- **Output naming:** offer clear names, keep-both, and destination choices; never silently overwrite originals or unrelated files.

## 3. Paper, print, engineering, and architecture drawings

- **Paper-size presets:** common US Letter and Legal, engineering ANSI A–E, architectural ARCH A–E, and ISO A-series such as A0–A4, where supported by the operation.
- **More page views:** single page, continuous scroll, facing pages, two-page spread, and side-by-side pages, with clear page order.
- **Large-sheet navigation:** smooth pan and zoom, zoom-to-region, fit-sheet, and return-to-previous-view for blueprints, plans, schematics, and maps.
- **Scale-aware measurement:** calibrate drawing scale first, then measure distance, perimeter, and area with visible units and a way to confirm calibration.
- **Drawing markups:** dimension lines, arrows, callouts, revision clouds, and color-coded comments alongside notes, highlights, and drawing tools.
- **PDF layers:** show or hide layers where the PDF contains them.
- **Drawing revision comparison:** align sheets and compare with a transparent overlay or side-by-side view; allow alignment adjustment when scale or position shifted.
- **Large-format printing:** print at actual size, fit to a chosen sheet, or tile across pages with overlap and alignment marks. Include ranges, orientation, scaling, and multiple pages per sheet.
- **Booklet printing:** provide layout preview and clear paper/duplex requirements.
- **Sheet sets:** group related drawings, navigate sheets, and preserve order.
- **Drawing information:** show sheet number, title, revision, dimensions, and page size when present.
- **CAD boundary:** do not imply PDFix edits CAD models; DWG and other CAD formats need separate decoder, licensing, and corpus evaluation.

## 4. Forms, signatures, and review

- **Create basic fillable forms:** add supported text, checkbox, radio, and choice fields, in addition to filling existing fields.
- **Improve form usability:** clearer labels, tab order, required-field guidance, supported fonts, and explanations for unsupported calculations/fields.
- **Form submission:** save a completed copy, print it, or export supported field data; explain unsupported fields.
- **Signature placement help:** identify likely signature/date/initial fields and suggest locations, but require confirmation of content and placement.
- **Reusable assets:** save user-approved signatures, initials, stamps, and common markups with clear local storage and deletion controls.
- **Broader annotations:** edit third-party annotations, threaded replies, and comment exchange only after preservation tests.
- **Annotation export:** offer a separate annotation summary or copy where verifiable.

## 5. Scanning, OCR, and information extraction

- **Scan from a device:** import from scanner/document camera, including multi-page scans where supported; preview, reorder, rotate, or remove pages before making a PDF.
- **Scan cleanup:** preview deskew, contrast/brightness cleanup, rotation, and proposed blank-page removal. Distinguish faint content from blank pages and allow undo.
- **Broader OCR:** add only tested bundled/installed languages; make language choice clear and show confidence as an estimate.
- **Uncertainty review:** locate uncertain words/lines on the scan, preserve page references, and require review before saving corrections.
- **Extract tables:** offer table-to-CSV/spreadsheet export only when recognition is suitable, with preview to catch misaligned rows and columns.
- **Searchable documents:** preserve scan images and explain when OCR reading order or recognition needs review.
- **Clear scan limits:** explain limits for handwriting, low resolution, skew, mixed languages, and complex reading order.

## 6. File formats, photos, and editing fidelity

Evaluate and add tested support for HEIC/HEIF (orientation and metadata choices), multipage TIFF, RTF, XLSX/PPTX preview/conversion, legacy DOC/XLS/PPT, and Apple Pages/Numbers/Keynote. Add a meaningful Markdown preview and structured table views for CSV/data files while retaining source editing. Complete real-file fixtures for XML, YAML, CSV, BMP, and uncommon image variants before claiming support. Clearly separate Open, Preview, Edit, and Convert for each format. Explain fidelity limits before conversion. Let users choose whether photo metadata/color profiles are kept or removed.

## 7. Navigation, search, and multi-file workflows

- **Search navigation:** match counts and next/previous controls.
- **Search selected files:** search only deliberately selected files; show filename and page for each result.
- **Quick action finder:** “What do you want to do?” search for sign, split, compress, OCR, compare, or convert.
- **Move pages across PDFs:** drag pages between open PDFs with a visible preview.
- **Page navigation:** jump by printed page label; edit bookmarks/table-of-contents entries; safely show internal link destinations.
- **Batch operations:** queue supported conversion, compression, rename, combine, and other verified actions with per-file progress/results, cancellation, output location, collision handling, and bounded resources.
- **Reusable workflows:** repeat reviewed sequences such as OCR → review → save copy or combine → number pages → print; show and allow editing of steps before running.
- **Recover interrupted jobs:** let users retry/discard failed or canceled jobs without confusing partial output for completed work.
- Search and batch features must not imply broad folder scanning.

## 8. Accessibility, quality checks, and inspection

- **Accessibility checks:** inspect tags, reading order, headings, links, and form labels; distinguish searchable OCR from accessible structure.
- **Guided accessibility repair:** offer fixes only when results can be validated; don’t promise automatic tagging makes a PDF fully accessible.
- **Document health report:** identify missing fonts, oversized images, broken links, unusual page sizes, unsupported features, and possible print problems; offer safe fixes only where verified.
- **Trustworthy file details:** show page dimensions/orientation/count, file size, text searchability, encryption state, and feature limits.
- **Accessible job status:** announce progress, failures, and cancellation to keyboard and screen-reader users.
- **Scalable interface:** test larger text, contrast, visible focus, keyboard navigation, and reduced motion throughout dialogs/workflows.
- **Print preview:** inspect prepared output, selected pages, paper, orientation, scaling, annotations, and rasterization before Windows handoff.
- Physical printer validation remains a release check; simulated preparation alone does not prove paper output.

## 9. Privacy, sharing, Windows, and AI

- **Share local copies:** provide Windows share handoff for a new copy. For cloud links/uploads, show service, account, destination, and permissions before sending.
- **Transfer history:** if online AI/sharing is added, show what files were sent, to which endpoint/service, and when; allow cleanup.
- **Optional AI providers/agents:** scope each request to selected files; show provider, model, endpoint, destination, and possible account charges before transfer.
- **Cited answers:** provide page/line references where available and distinguish source text from generated explanation.
- **Read-only AI by default:** treat document contents as untrusted; prevent automatic saving/exporting/overwriting/tool use. Require separate approval and a reviewable result for changes.
- **Connection controls:** test, select, and remove connections; store secrets using Windows-backed secure storage and fail closed if unavailable.
- **Hermes:** evaluate its documented HTTP API before implementing.
- **Harness:** defer until the exact product/interface is identified.
- **Windows lifecycle:** installer, uninstaller, updates, optional file associations, and Open with PDFix.
- **Release readiness:** security, licensing, dependency/SBOM, performance, clean-machine install, and real-file corpus reviews.

## 10. Later candidates and first-release boundaries

Later candidates: online signature requests/tracking, shared/cloud review, online form response collection, PDF/A or PDF/X validation, tagged-PDF validation, accessibility repair, and Bates numbering. Each needs a clear user need and reviewed engine/service before it appears as working.

Keep bulk signature/payment workflows, PDF portfolios, barcode fields, advanced print-shop color/trapping, geospatial/3D measurement, embedded multimedia, presentation generation, and CAD model editing out of the initial scope unless the direction changes.

## Current product features (not missing)

The project documents a Windows-first local Electron workspace; picker and drag/drop; recents/favorites; PDF reading, search, selection, print preparation, outlines and saved reading positions; page organization, crop/resize, page ranges and documented automatic splitting; PDF comparison; PDFix markups; supported AcroForm filling and confirmed visual signatures; local English OCR with review; basic DOCX/TXT/source editing; version/recovery tools; and one-image-to-one-page PDF creation. Each has limits; some support applies only to tested subsets.

# PDFix product plan

PDFix is a Windows-first, local document workspace for people who need to read a manual, fix a scan, organize paperwork, or understand a file without learning a professional publishing suite.

## Users and problems

- Individuals: readable documents, searchable scans, simple edits, private copies.
- Office staff: dependable page organization, form filling, conversion previews, clear output names.
- Researchers: selectable text, source references, search across deliberately selected files.
- People using assistive technology: keyboard access, scalable controls, readable layouts and progress announcements.

## Product principles

1. Preserve originals. Every output is a new copy; never silently overwrite.
2. Explain capabilities per format: Open, Preview, Edit, Convert. Opening a file is not proof of editability.
3. Make processing local by default. File content must not cause network requests.
4. Explain risks before lossy conversion, rasterization, redaction, remote sharing or agent access.
5. Show actual progress and failures. No fabricated recent files, connections, OCR or AI answers.
6. Offer plain actions, using the supplied HTML's mint palette, restrained sidebar and familiar document controls.

### Two-way conversions and Apple photo support — user decision, October 8, 2026

Adopted at the user's explicit request: ensure every core supported format operates reliably in **both directions** (Format ↔ PDF), and add native support for Apple iPhone/iPad photo formats:

1. **Two-way conversion requirements:**
   - **Documents:** `.docx` ↔ PDF, `.rtf` ↔ PDF, and `.txt` ↔ PDF must both import into editable formats and export to verified PDF copies.
   - **Markdown (`.md`):** Two-way support must include (a) **Styled Markdown → PDF** (rendering `#` headings, `**bold**`, bullet lists, and tables as formatted document pages, not only raw monospace code blocks) and (b) **PDF → Clean Markdown** (1-click export of structured text, headings, and tables for use with LLMs, Obsidian, and Notion).
   - **Spreadsheets (`.csv`, `.xlsx`):** In addition to PDF table extraction → CSV/XLSX, add direct **Sheet/Workbook → PDF** export from the workbook workspace with formatted grid lines and page bounds.
   - **Standard Images:** `.png` ↔ PDF, `.jpg`/`.jpeg` ↔ PDF, `.webp` ↔ PDF, and `.bmp` ↔ PDF with two-way conversion (adding WebP and BMP to the image export dropdown).

2. **Apple photo formats (HEIC / HEIF):**
   - Provide intake for Apple iOS photos (`.heic` / `.heif`) to convert directly into PDF pages alongside standard JPEG/PNG scans.
   - Support Live Photo component extraction (still photo frame) and export.
   - Evaluate a licensed, contained local decoder (such as Windows Imaging Component WIC integration or bundled WebAssembly libheif) so users can drop iPhone photos directly into PDFix without conversion warnings.

### Workspace

Native picker and drag/drop open real files. Recent files and favorites persist locally, can be filtered and forgotten, and stale paths yield an actionable error. Unsupported, corrupt, empty and excessive files are handled without crashing. Whole-file operations retain a 100 MiB budget. The October 7 large-PDF reading route allows file-backed, on-demand opening up to the current 1 GiB viewer budget, subject to RAM/disk admission and explicit per-operation capabilities; larger or resource-heavy files receive a specific reason. Actual large-file performance acceptance remains pending. No recursive directory indexing. Support matrix is visible from Home.

### PDF reading

Local PDF.js renders actual pages, thumbnails and selectable text. Users navigate, zoom, fit width, search with page references, copy page text and print all pages. Password prompts permit reading only with a supplied password and respect document permissions. Encrypted originals are never rewritten through an ignore-encryption option. Scan detection is a heuristic per page, not an OCR success claim.

### PDF fixes

Ordered page list supports rotation, removal, duplication, extraction, combining and splitting; output is reopened and verified. Annotations include highlight, underline, drawing, text, notes/comments; output retains them. Supported AcroForms and saved signatures are separately tested; XFA/digital signature certification is out of scope initially. OCR runs offline with bundled engine/language data, offers editable recognized text, preserves page coordinates and produces a searchable copy. Compression explicitly previews actual size and quality. The initial lossless/optional JPEG workflow preserves supported reachable structures and non-image content, verifies real output and discloses larger results; broader corpus and resource hardening remain gates. Any future raster mode must disclose lost text/forms. Redaction reconstructs sanitized output, excludes original streams/metadata/attachments, and passes extraction, object inspection and visual tests. Password protection uses a reviewed engine; no DRM bypass.

### Documents and images

Plain UTF-8 text, Markdown and data formats first. Familiar page editor offers headings, lists, bold/italic, undo/redo where the source representation supports them. Plain text must not be marketed as preserving rich formatting. Image preview and conversion operate locally. DOCX import warns about fidelity; RTF and office conversions require corpus tests. XLSX/PPTX initially preview/convert only. HEIC/TIFF require reviewed decoders. Legacy and Apple formats stay unavailable until verified.

### AI and agents

Models and agents are separate connection kinds. Local and custom OpenAI-compatible models can be tested and removed, with selected model displayed. Hermes uses its documented HTTP API; a loopback agent can still send context to its upstream provider and must never be labeled local-only on address alone. Harness is ambiguous: defer a named integration until its product/interface is identified. Each request selects files and shows endpoint and data destination; explicit consent precedes remote transfer. Context is text with page/line references, never broad filesystem access. Secrets use Windows-backed Electron safeStorage; fail closed if unavailable. AI results cannot invoke save/export/edit commands.

### Reliability and release

Job cancellation and memory/page limits, recovery for edits, keyboard workflows, accessible names/focus, clear errors. Windows installer and portable build, clean-machine smoke tests, notices/SBOM, dependency/security review and verified format corpus are release gates. Signing/distribution require owner credentials and a later explicit publishing decision.

This document defines targets; `FORMAT-SUPPORT.md` and `PHASE-LOG.md` record verified behavior. The existing original-safety and local-processing rules apply throughout.

## Work protection and privacy

- **R01 Recovery and versions:** debounce autosave, preserve undo/redo during editing, recover after an interrupted process, and retain bounded local versions. Show timestamps and a preview before restoring. Restoring must checkpoint the current state first and must never rewrite the source file. Bind recovery to source fingerprints so externally changed files do not silently receive stale edits. Explain retention, size limits, unencrypted local content and how to clear it.
- **R02 Leaving unsaved work:** wait for pending recovery writes before closing or switching files. If recovery fails, keep the editor available with export/retry options; never silently discard unsaved edits. Offer a clear discard action only after a warning. Converted/edited outputs use a native location chooser and save as a new copy.
- **R03 Cleanup:** users can clear recent metadata, recovery/version content and temporary job files independently. Show what will be removed and what remains. Never delete original or exported documents. Diagnostic logs must exclude document text, passwords and secrets. Display online-transfer history when AI/cloud features exist.
- **R04 Recoverable operations:** retain recoverable inputs and staged outputs before risky changes. A failed or canceled conversion leaves the original intact, and users can review or discard its output. Clearly distinguish rotation of a view from rotation of saved pages.
- **R05 Output collisions:** explain duplicate output names and offer another name/folder or an explicit keep-both operation. Never overwrite an original or alias. Replacing an unrelated existing output, if later supported, requires a specific user choice and a recoverable backup; the current exclusive writer continues refusing replacements.

## Reading, selection, comparison and printing

- **R06 Navigation and views:** show document outline/bookmarks, page labels and internal links; support personal bookmarks, single page, continuous scroll, two-page spread, fit width/page and temporary view rotation. Lazy loading, bounded canvases, progress and cancellation remain mandatory for large files.
- **R07 Complex selection:** show readable text with page references, preserve sensible row/column order where verified, and offer a bounded local region when automatic selection fails. Columns, tables, footnotes, captions and rotated text require corpus tests; never promise perfect reading order from arbitrary PDF content streams.
- **R08 Safe links and attachments:** identify the destination of external links and ask before opening a website. Do not execute PDF scripts. List embedded files with type/size warnings and save only to a user-chosen location; never auto-open or auto-run extracted content. ZIP traversal, bombs, device names and symlinks require safe handling before any extraction feature ships.
- **R09 Compare:** open two user-selected PDFs side by side with independent and linked navigation. Compare page count/order, extracted text and page artwork; scanned pages require visual comparison. Explain alignment and OCR uncertainty, highlight additions/removals, and avoid equating an OCR-only difference with a proven source change. Source/output comparison is available before accepting a lossy conversion.
- **R10 Printing:** preview exactly the prepared output, select page ranges, paper size, orientation and fit/actual-size scaling, and disclose raster resolution or annotation flattening. Detect invalid ranges, clipped content and unsupported print settings. OS cancellation must clean up temporary pages. Physical printer review remains a release gate.

## Scans, forms, signatures and annotations

- **R11 OCR:** let users choose among actually bundled/installed languages, review and correct recognized text, locate uncertain words/lines on the scan, and see confidence as an engine estimate rather than accuracy. Warn about handwriting, poor scans and complex reading order. Only advertise tested languages. English recognition/review/searchable output is already scoped and verified; broad quality/language support is not.
- **R12 Scan cleanup:** offer viewable rotation, deskew, contrast cleanup and proposed blank-page removal before OCR. Preview every destructive change, allow undo, distinguish blank from faint content, and verify searchable output against reviewed text. Preserve the original.
- **R13 Forms:** support a verified subset of AcroForms with values, required-field guidance, usable tab order and supported calculations. Never execute arbitrary form JavaScript. Identify unsupported calculations/XFA clearly; preserve values and appearances when exporting. Scanned forms use user-positioned text/checkmarks first; automatic field detection remains an experimental proposal until tested.
- **R14 Signatures:** distinguish typed/drawn/stored visual signatures from cryptographic signatures. A pasted signature image is not certificate validation. Detect existing signature fields, show validity as unknown unless a reviewed validator actually checks it, and warn/refuse changes that may invalidate a signature. Here is the complete, categorized breakdown of everything where **Adobe Acrobat Pro beats PDFix**, based on Adobe’s actual enterprise capabilities and the explicit exclusions, deferrals, and gaps listed in the PDFix catalog:

---

### 1. Legal, Cryptographic & Enterprise Signatures
* **Certified PKI Signatures:** Adobe natively integrates with the **AATL (Adobe Approved Trust List)** and **EUTL (European Union Trust List)**. When you sign in Adobe with a hardware token, SmartCard, or digital certificate, the PDF is cryptographically sealed, tamper-evident, and legally recognized in court under ESIGN, UETA, and eIDAS.
  * *PDFix status:* **Explicitly excluded for initial release.** Only supports visual stamps and drawn/typed visual marks, which have zero cryptographic proof.
* **Cloud Signature Routing & Audit Trails (Adobe Sign):** Adobe offers multi-party signature workflows, automated routing orders, authentication challenges (SMS/email OTP), and legally binding audit logs.
  * *PDFix status:* **Excluded/deferred (F39).** No external signature dispatch, no recipient tracking, and no bulk signature/payment pipelines.

---

### 2. Print-Shop, Prepress & Color Management
* **Commercial Prepress & Preflight:** Adobe includes the industry-standard Preflight engine (Callas Software), capable of automated inspection, color-profile conversion, and syntax verification for commercial printers.
* **Color Trapping & Plate Separation Preview:** Adobe allows commercial printers to inspect individual CMYK and Pantone/spot color plates, overprint simulations, dot gain, and color trapping.
* **Print Standards (PDF/X):** Acrobat Pro can validate and enforce PDF/X-1a, PDF/X-3, PDF/X-4, and PDF/X-6 compliance.
  * *PDFix status:* **Explicitly excluded/deferred (M10.02, F40).** PDFix explicitly excludes advanced print-shop color management/trapping and has deferred PDF/X verification.

---

### 3. Standards Compliance & Archival (PDF/A, PDF/E)
* **Turnkey Archival Conversion (PDF/A):** Adobe can analyze arbitrary PDFs and convert them into compliant ISO standards (PDF/A-1b, PDF/A-2b, PDF/A-3u) with embedded ICC profiles, device-independent colors, and embedded font subsets.
  * *PDFix status:* **Deferred (M10.01, F40).** PDFix treats standards compliance as a future candidate and explicitly notes that neither a visual match nor a file extension guarantees standard compliance.

---

### 4. Accessibility Remediation (Section 508 / PDF/UA / WCAG)
* **Industrial Tag Tree Editing:** Adobe Acrobat Pro contains a full Tag Tree Editor, Reading Order Panel, and Touch Up Reading Order tools required to make PDFs legally compliant for blind/low-vision users.
* **Automated Accessibility Auditing:** Adobe generates detailed compliance reports for PDF/UA and Section 508, allowing bulk artifact tagging, alt-text assignment, and table header mapping.
  * *PDFix status:* **Basic only (M08.01–02, F30).** PDFix only offers basic structural inspection and limited guided repairs; it lacks a full tag-tree remediation environment.

---

### 5. Advanced Forms & Dynamic Scripting
* **Dynamic XFA Forms:** Adobe supports complex, reflowing XML Forms Architecture (XFA) used by federal governments, defense agencies, and healthcare providers.
* **Embedded Acrobat JavaScript Engine:** Adobe executes rich JavaScript inside forms for live validation, arithmetic recalculations, button actions, and formatting.
* **2D Barcode Fields:** Acrobat dynamically generates paper 2D barcodes that encode filled form data as the user types.
* **Database & Web Submissions:** Adobe forms can submit payloads directly to web endpoints or corporate databases.
  * *PDFix status:* **Hard exclusion (M04.01–03, M10.02).** PDFix **refuses to run PDF scripts/macros** for security, does not support XFA forms, and excludes barcode fields entirely.

---

### 6. PDF Portfolios & Container Formats
* **Multi-File PDF Portfolios:** Adobe can bundle dozens of different files (Word, Excel, CAD, video, other PDFs) inside an interactive, navigable 3D or grid-based portfolio package.
  * *PDFix status:* **Explicitly excluded (M10.02).** PDFix cannot create or navigate PDF portfolios.

---

### 7. 3D Models, Geospatial Maps & Multimedia
* **Interactive 3D PDF:** Adobe natively renders embedded 3D CAD models (U3D and PRC formats), allowing users to rotate parts, create cross-section slices, measure 3D geometries, and toggle part assemblies.
* **Geospatial PDF (GIS):** Acrobat recognizes embedded coordinate metadata (latitude/longitude) and allows GIS measurements.
* **Embedded Multimedia:** Acrobat plays embedded audio, video, and rich interactive media.
  * *PDFix status:* **Explicitly excluded (M10.02).** PDFix excludes 3D models, geospatial measurements, and embedded media playback.

---

### 8. Enterprise Rights Management (DRM) & Policy Control
* **Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) Document Security:** Organizations can enforce central DRM policies—revoking access to a document remotely even after it has been downloaded, expiring access on specific dates, or restricting printing.
  * *PDFix status:* **Explicitly excluded (M10.02).** Only supports basic local password encryption (open/permission passwords); zero enterprise DRM support.

---

### 9. Multi-Platform Ecosystem & Browser Sharing
* **Cloud Link Reviews (No Software Required):** Adobe allows you to generate a web link where anyone on a Mac, Chromebook, phone, or PC can comment on a PDF in a web browser without installing anything.
* **Mobile Ecosystem & "Liquid Mode":** Adobe has mature iOS/Android apps with reflowing "Liquid Mode" for reading documents on phones.
  * *PDFix status:* **Windows desktop only (F36).** Built strictly for Windows; browser-based shared review and cloud links are deferred candidates.

---

### 10. Engine Maturity on Corrupted/Wild PDFs
* **30 Years of Real-World Parser Tolerances:** Acrobat can reliably open broken, malformed, 1990s PostScript-derived, or non-spec PDFs produced by hundreds of different third-party generators without crashing.
  * *PDFix status:* **Under active development.** A large corpus of adversarial and broken files has not yet been accepted or certified through runtime release gates (F42).

The markup writer keeps foreign annotation dictionaries in the PDF context and edits only annotations it recognizes as PDFix-owned. It does not prove foreign dictionary/appearance/resource equality, NM identity stability, reply topology, status history, custom-field retention, author/date preservation or Revu behavior. Flattening converts PDFix visual marks to page artwork; notes remain annotations. Flattened artwork is not an editable markup exchange.

# Local certificate signing progress

This implements initial PDF approval signing with an explicitly selected local Windows RSA certificate/private-key provider. It is a working source implementation toward A02, with syntax/native compilation completed and runtime acceptance pending. It does not claim complete Acrobat, PAdES, certification, multiple-signature, trust-service or legal-signature equivalence.

## Supported flow

1. Inspect the immutable opened source inside the fixed document AppContainer. Require a complete PDF/security/signature inventory, a single classic-xref revision, no encryption, no existing signature fields/dictionaries, and no certification, field locks, seed constraints, usage-rights permissions or XFA. Cross-reference subsections, object identities/offsets, complete inventory, Root and Size are checked before adding a revision. Xref streams, hybrid files and historical incremental sources are explicitly unsupported in this first slice.
2. Enumerate RSA certificates from Windows `CurrentUser/My` read-only, including certificate subject, issuer, serial, fingerprint, validity dates, RSA key size and registered key-provider name. Only provider metadata and the public certificate are read during enumeration; private-key handles are not acquired. Expired/not-yet-valid certificates or restrictive key usage remain visible but cannot be selected for signing. The user must choose a certificate and review its details and the document before the Sign action.
3. Prepare a new incremental revision inside the document engine. Every original source byte remains an exact prefix. New indirect objects contain the approval signature, an invisible AcroForm signature field, an updated form and a new catalog. The appended classic xref and trailer point to the prior revision with `/Prev`, retaining `/Info` and `/ID`. The signature uses `/Filter /Adobe.PPKLite`, `/SubFilter /adbe.pkcs7.detached`, a fixed-width `/ByteRange` and a 32 KiB hex `/Contents` reservation. Reason and location are UTF-16 PDF hex strings. No original page streams, keys or source file are rewritten.
4. Parent validation checks the original prefix hash, complete output hash, exact excluded Contents framing, all-zero reservation, full-file ByteRange, selected certificate fingerprint, reviewed metadata and SHA-256 over the exact covered bytes. CMS signed attributes are fixed canonical DER containing only `content-type=id-data` and `message-digest=SHA-256(covered bytes)`; the parent reconstructs all 77 attribute bytes rather than trusting a document-provided signing request.
5. Only the explicit Sign action launches `CertificateSigning.cs` with the fixed `sign-v1` protocol. It receives the selected certificate ID/provider and bounded hashes/signed attributes, never PDF bytes, paths, algorithms, commands or private-key material. It reopens the selected CurrentUser certificate, rechecks its dates, key usage, fingerprint and provider, reconstructs the signed attributes, and acquires a key handle with `CryptAcquireCertificatePrivateKey` using `ALLOW_NCRYPT`, `COMPARE_KEY` and `NO_HEALING`. Provider PIN/consent UI is allowed at this stage. RSA SHA-256 PKCS#1 v1.5 uses CNG `NCryptSignHash` or legacy CryptoAPI `CryptCreateHash`/`CryptSetHashParam`/`CryptSignHash`. CAPI little-endian signature bytes are reversed for CMS. The provider result is verified against the selected certificate's public key before return. No private key is exported or imported, and the code never requests a provider-specific key file.
6. The document engine assembles detached CMS SignedData using the selected leaf certificate and its exact issuer/serial, then fills only the reserved Contents bytes. It independently reopens the full new PDF through the existing certificate inspection implementation, reparses CMS/ByteRange/Contents, and verifies the signature and signed digest over the actual output. The result must have exactly one source-bound signature covering the entire current file, with the selected signer fingerprint and expected signature object. Parent validation checks this receipt and independently compares covered-byte hashes before retaining a saveable output. Raw DER certificate bundles are removed from the renderer receipt.
7. The user saves the verified signed PDF as a new copy. The native service retains sealed output bytes and source/token bindings; renderer-provided arbitrary bytes are never used as the save source. Cancellation, source departure or discard invalidates the retained copy. Source fingerprint fencing and collision-safe copy saving are also enforced by the main-process integration.

## Provider and containment boundaries

The document parser and CMS authoring code run only in the fixed document AppContainer. The Windows certificate provider adapter runs with normal user certificate/key-provider access and is not a document parser. Registered CAPI/CNG smart-card, token and HSM providers can participate through their Windows handles when they support the requested RSA operation; a registered certificate does not establish connected hardware, PIN availability or successful signing. Provider-specific runtime compatibility remains untested. Unsupported provider behavior fails closed without a signature receipt.

The native helper accepts only fixed `list-v1` and `sign-v1` operations, reads bounded stdin, returns a SHA-256-bound response, and has no shell/path request surface. Certificates are bounded to 64 KiB, enumeration to 100 certificates and 1 MiB combined DER, requests to 16 KiB and output to 2 MiB. A one-process Windows job caps memory at 256 MiB and CPU time at 20 seconds. The parent allows 30 seconds for enumeration or two minutes for an explicit signing/PIN interaction, enforces output limits and waits for observed process exit. If termination is not observed within five seconds, the provider remains closed and no output is released. Provider UI or external vendor components may have their own lifecycle; physical-device and cancellation acceptance remain pending.

Executable SHA-256, strict manifest policy and an explicitly reviewed source SHA-256 pin are checked before launching the fixed helper. The build refuses a changed native source until the pin is updated. The selected certificate metadata and public DER are retained in main-process memory, so renderer input can select only a certificate from that inventory. Sign responses must match the exact reviewed certificate, source hash, prepared-copy hash, covered-content hash and signed attributes.

## Explicit limitations

- Only initial, invisible RSA 2048–8192-bit SHA-256 PKCS#1 v1.5 approval signatures are authored. ECDSA/RSA-PSS signing, visible signature appearances, certificate enrollment, certificate import, local key generation and key export are not implemented.
- Existing signatures and signature fields, prior incremental revisions, certification/DocMDP/FieldMDP, locks/seed constraints, encrypted documents and xref streams are refused. Supporting multiple signatures requires authenticated revision/modification-policy handling rather than weakening those checks.
- CMS includes the selected leaf certificate. Intermediate certificates are not downloaded or embedded; subsequent chain building can use separately available local Windows certificate material.
- Certificate identity displayed during selection is a certificate claim. Signing does not establish chain trust, revocation status, Adobe/EU trust-list membership, document-signing EKU/issuance policy, trusted signing time, long-term validation or legal status. # Certificate signature validation progress

This implements a contained, read-only certificate inspection slice toward the full PDFix document workspace. It is not a claim of complete certificate, PAdES, signing, trust-service or specialist PDF support.

## Implemented

- The fixed `certificate-inspect` operation accepts only source PDF bytes and no paths, URLs or document-supplied operations. `PdfCertificateService` extends `ContainedServiceContext`; its inert output validator checks the original source SHA-256 and byte length. The original is never rewritten.
- A bounded lexical source walk skips comments, literal strings and length-delimited streams. It binds a unique indirect signature dictionary to the parsed PDF dictionary. Four direct ByteRange integers must begin at zero, remain in bounds and exclude exactly that dictionary's direct hexadecimal Contents token. The covered revision must terminate at EOF. Appended bytes are reported as uncovered; a previous-revision integrity result does not certify the current document.
- Detached `adbe.pkcs7.detached` and a restricted `ETSI.CAdES.detached` subset verify CMS SignedData, detached id-data, a unique signer certificate binding, signed message-digest and the cryptographic signature. Supported digests are SHA-256/384/512; algorithms are RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 with 2048–8192-bit keys, and ECDSA on P-256/P-384/P-521. Node's native crypto verifies signatures and reads X.509 certificates.
- Signed attributes use the exact encoded bytes with the IMPLICIT context tag replaced by SET per RFC 5652 section 5.4. Definite minimal DER lengths, bounded depth/nodes, SET order, single-valued unique attributes and the content-type/message-digest pair are required. Supported attributes are content-type, message-digest, signing-time and restricted signingCertificateV2. ESS certificate hash and optional exact issuer/serial bindings are checked. Unknown signed attributes are unsupported, never silently ignored.
- The modal displays signature integrity, byte coverage, signer certificate claims and fingerprint, claimed signing time, and current certificate date validity. The offline Windows certificate chain is a separate result, including the chain subjects, issuers, SHA-256 fingerprints, validity dates, Windows error flags and base-policy status. Trusted timestamps, revocation and document modification policy remain explicitly not checked. A trusted offline base chain never produces an overall "valid PDF signature" conclusion.
- Only signatures whose covered bytes and CMS signature passed integrity verification release a signer-first DER certificate bundle from the contained engine. Parent validation bounds each certificate to 64 KiB, each bundle to 128 KiB and 32 certificates, checks canonical base64 and complete DER outer framing, rejects duplicate certificate hashes, and binds the first DER certificate SHA-256 to the reported CMS signer. Internal reports are limited to 6 MiB. The contained source hash and byte length are checked before any native trust operation. Raw certificate bundles are removed before renderer IPC.
- `CertificateTrust.cs` accepts one fixed stdin protocol and a fixed operation argument, with no PDF bytes, file paths, URLs or arbitrary operations. Certificates must be single DER X.509 certificates; PKCS#12/key containers and other certificate-store encodings are refused. It creates an ephemeral memory store of supplied candidates, calls Windows `CertGetCertificateChain` at the current time, and runs `CERT_CHAIN_POLICY_BASE` without ignored errors. The supplied certificates are never added to the trusted root store. Trust additionally requires the final chain certificate SHA-256 to match an existing CurrentUser or LocalMachine Windows Root certificate, all chain/element errors and base-policy errors to be zero, all certificate dates to cover inspection time, and the signer key usage to permit digital signature or nonrepudiation when present.
- Offline behavior is explicit: `CERT_CHAIN_CACHE_ONLY_URL_RETRIEVAL`, `CERT_CHAIN_DISABLE_AUTH_ROOT_AUTO_UPDATE`, `CERT_CHAIN_DISABLE_AIA` and `CERT_CHAIN_REVOCATION_CHECK_CACHE_ONLY` are set; no revocation-check or peer-trust flag is enabled. Local Windows stores and cached chain material are consulted; the adapter never downloads issuer certificates, CRLs, OCSP, trust lists or roots, and never modifies certificate stores. Locally installed enterprise or user roots are eligible, so a passing result describes this computer's trust configuration, not Adobe/EU trust-list membership or universal identity assurance.
- The native helper has a one-process Windows job, 256 MiB memory and 15-second process CPU limit; its parent applies a 30-second wall-clock limit, bounded stdin/stdout, no shell, and hidden-window launch. Cancellation waits for observed exit. Failure to observe termination within five seconds permanently closes that service and withholds its result. The application checks a strict helper manifest, executable SHA-256 and a pinned source SHA-256 before launch. The build refuses changed native source until its explicit pin is reviewed and updated. The reply includes the exact request SHA-256, source SHA-256 and signer fingerprint; every result is shape-checked and recomputed for consistency before release.

## Conservative refusals and remaining work

Encrypted PDFs, direct/compressed signature dictionaries, repeated definitions of the signature object, indirect stream lengths, duplicate dictionary keys, malformed syntax, alternate signature subfilters, BER/indefinite encodings, unknown signed attributes, multiple CMS signers, unsupported keys/algorithms and ambiguous certificate bindings are reported as unsupported. Inventory includes parsed orphan signature objects; it does not assert that a signature field is active or visible. No historical object graph or DocMDP/FieldMDP permissions are validated. PDF parser differential analysis remains specialist work.

Remaining: application-managed trust anchors and Adobe/EU trust lists; document-signing EKU, issuance and signature-policy validation beyond the Windows base policy; offline and consented online OCSP/CRL paths; authenticated RFC 3161 timestamps and long-term validation evidence; broader CMS/PAdES/ESS and RSA-PSS support; certificate signing and hardware key integration; incremental revision policy analysis; specialist PDF encodings and additional standards. CTL-linked multiple-simple-chain paths are conservatively unavailable. Expired or not-yet-valid certificates fail current-time chain validation even if signature mathematics pass; signer-claimed signing time is never used to backdate trust. No document-supplied URL, certificate AIA URL, CRL location, arbitrary file or external executable is accessed.

The native orchestration service is `desktop/pdf-combine-workflow-service.cjs`; continuation controls, receipt validation and final-source mapping live in the existing `src/pdf-combine-workspace.js`, `src/pdf-combine-model.js` and stylesheet. Main/preload route wiring is owned by the integration change.

## Native trust and execution

`PdfCombineWorkflowService.build(sessionId, trustedSources, token, {combine, steps})` accepts the same native-retained original snapshots as standalone combination, an exact inspected combination map, and one or two existing raw reorder/Bates step definitions. Sources are not supplied by renderer bytes or paths. The service calls `PdfCombineService`, retrieves its sealed native output internally, closes that stage, and supplies that exact output as the trusted source for `DocumentWorkflowService`. The existing preserving reorder and decoration codecs run inside their fixed contained engine routes; there is no new unrestricted parser or renderer reconstruction route.

The final seal binds original per-source metadata/hashes, combination selection/hash and object manifests, expanded editable settings, ordered continuation receipts, exact input/output SHA-256 at every stage, final original-page/object mappings, final bytes and a canonical whole-receipt SHA-256. Saving asks the native owner for `output(sessionId, trustedSources, token)` and never accepts bytes from the renderer. The service rechecks retained source fingerprints, receipt hashes, ordered stage hashes, page mappings and the precise Bates identifier sequence before releasing a copy to the native save route.

Each stage closes before its successor starts. Intermediate preview copies and stage seals are zeroed after use. Cancel/discard invalidate the matching final seal, cancel the active owning stage, await the complete orchestration promise and observed contained cleanup, and stay closed if cleanup fails. Disposal awaits the same completion boundary. A new build always starts from the retained originals, including when the user edits or reorders continuation steps.

## Editable user flow

The standalone combination flow is unchanged when no continuation cards are added. Users may add one reorder and one Bates card, edit settings, move either card up/down, or remove it. Reorder accepts a complete permutation of up to 500 current physical pages and provides a reverse action; identity reorder is rejected before processing. Bates uses the existing standard-font, position, size, color, opacity, inset, ASCII prefix/suffix, start/digit and up-to-100-current-pages contract.

The final source map composes combination and reorder. Bates page ownership is composed at the point where its step runs: moving numbering before/after reorder can assign the same identifiers to different originals. The final PDF is independently opened with PDF.js and compared to the correctly mapped original pages for geometry, annotations, widget values/namespaces, local link destinations and grouped bookmark hierarchy/targets. Expected Bates strings are checked in text extracted from their final mapped pages and shown in the page-review status.

Actual originals and final output render side by side. Every final page must be viewed and the continuation order, Bates identifiers/possible overlap, source mapping and preservation limits acknowledged before the token-only final save is enabled. Edits invalidate the output and review evidence. Asynchronous hash/load boundaries and generation fences prevent cancelled builds from installing a stale preview; close waits for native and preview cleanup before releasing the editor guard.

## Remaining scope and evidence

Combination retains its explicit full-source-only and unsupported-structure refusals; partial extraction/duplication and broader semantic merging remain unfinished. Continuations currently support one reorder and one Bates step, using the existing shared workflow service contract. No general-purpose arbitrary operation graph, automatic collision detection for Bates already present in originals, page-artwork collision proof, sanitation, certification or proprietary PDF application fidelity claim is added. Saved combined workflow definitions/recovery are outside this slice.

Only source inspection and `node --check` were performed. No tests, PDF parsing/execution, runtime/UI/native/device validation, fixtures or new tests were run. Product PDF.js and native reopen verification described above is implemented behavior, not executed acceptance evidence. Root integration compilation follows source freeze.

# Disk-backed page-at-a-time PDF opening

October 10, 2026. User authorized implementation after the large drawing was still refused by the full-document memory estimate. This is actual integrated code, not a planned-only entry. It is not evidence that the user's drawing opens correctly or that arbitrary PDFs have no lag.

## Opening and rendering changes

- An immutable large-PDF disk snapshot can be created without the previous 1 GiB input refusal or full-document RAM refusal. File length must be a supported positive safe integer and the filesystem must have room for the snapshot. The existing read-only fingerprint and source-change checks remain.
- When the full viewer's estimate is above available memory, or a source exceeds its 1 GiB buffer budget, opening selects a disk-backed paged descriptor instead of sending the full source length to PDF.js. Ordinary ranged reading remains available when admitted within its budgets.
- A PDF with more than 500 physical pages can switch to paged reading, including a bounded in-memory original. Personal positions/bookmarks can refer to these larger physical page numbers; their count and title length remain bounded.
- A private main-process capability streams the immutable snapshot into an isolated persistent input slot using a 256 KiB buffer. The isolated copy is reused for subsequent page requests. This initially uses two temporary disk copies for large sources; preparing them and checking their fingerprints requires sequential I/O proportional to file size.
- A distinct pinned Windows AppContainer broker profile admits disk-backed input without the old 100 MiB native-input bound. Existing native and document profiles retain their previous limits. The new profile only grants reading of input/runtime and writing of one output slot; parent tracking, observed broker exit, process/memory/time restrictions and file watchdogs remain.
- The contained qpdf engine checks encryption status and page count, then creates a private one-page working PDF on demand. Renderer workers receive only that small PDF and validate its source identity and SHA-256. The original file is not rewritten or saved.
- The frontend serializes page work, deduplicates requests, cancels superseded work and keeps at most two page workers. Preview pixels are reduced. Physical page number/Previous/Next, text selection, readable text, local notes, bookmarks and fullscreen remain available.
- Loading status and a Cancel loading control are available. A first-page failure keeps the document's physical navigation available so a different page can be attempted. Native sessions are released when their source is released, the renderer ends or the app exits. Recognized interrupted native staging has a bounded cleanup pass; unknown folders are left untouched.

## Boundaries still requiring work

- “Any size” means input size alone no longer triggers the previous fixed large-file rejection in the disk-backed fallback. It is not a guarantee to open every PDF on every computer. Disk space, safe filesystem lengths, staging time, PDF structure and native/parser/rendering resources still apply.
- Native parsing remains limited to 512 MiB and a 115-second watchdog per command. Each extracted working page is at most 32 MiB. A complex page or huge object graph can exceed these limits even with a small input. Such failure is reported rather than running an unrestricted parser.
- Encrypted/permission-controlled files are refused in paged mode pending an owner-authorized password/permission-preserving implementation. Regular supported password opening remains on the ordinary viewer path.
- This mode does not yet support whole-document editing/export, printing, document-wide search/text tools, continuous/facing view, background thumbnails, original outline/page labels, original link destinations, layer controls, signature validation or document-wide review panels. Controls are disabled with scope explanations; working-page metadata/signatures must not be presented as the original document's evidence.
- qpdf page copying is intended to retain page content/resources and geometry, but blueprint accuracy, annotations, optional content defaults, transparency, fonts, cropped/rotated sheets, huge raster pages and accessibility behavior remain unverified. Existing viewer image-size limits can affect difficult raster pages and require later fidelity work.
- Native parsing repeats per requested page and can have substantial latency. A persistent parser, bounded extracted-page cache or carefully bounded nearby-page prefetch are possible later improvements after measuring the actual drawing; they were not implemented here.
- No PDF/runtime/UI/device/performance tests or new fixtures were executed. Only source syntax and compilation checks were performed. The user's approximately 156,000 KB engineering file is the first required runtime acceptance case; record first useful page, navigation, cancellation, source integrity, geometry and peak memory before calling the blocker resolved.

# Contained DOCX table-grid inspection

Saved 2026-10-04. The fixed `document-table-grids` operation invokes `desktop/document-grid-import.cjs` only inside the packaged Windows AppContainer document engine. The parent never opens DOCX ZIP/XML to derive table layout and has no direct or worker fallback.

`desktop/document-grid-service.cjs` exports:

```js
await inspectDocumentTableGrids(id,store.source(id));
await cancelDocumentTableGrids(id); // ID can be omitted to cancel the current job
await disposeDocumentTableGrids();
await restartDocumentTableGrids(); // replaces only after observed safe disposal
await documentTableGridStatus();
```

Main must use an opened FileStore DOCX source. The service verifies its immutable fingerprint, makes an owned snapshot and retains source ID/generation cancellation fences. It uses the shared one-job-per-family lifecycle, two-job process cap, observed broker exit/profile cleanup and permanent unsafe-failure closure. The shared package status cache remains display-only; every launch still checks pinned broker/runtime bytes.

The child and parent require the exact compact inert report:

```js
{
  version:1,
  sourceSha256:'64 lowercase hexadecimal characters',
  tables:[{
    key:'table-1', // exact one-based source ordinal, not an association guess
    rows:1,
    columns:2,
    widthsTwips:[3000,3000], // null when unavailable; otherwise 1..30000 each
    signature:'64 lowercase hexadecimal characters', // null when unavailable
    reason:null // bounded explicit explanation when layout/identity is unavailable
  }],
  notices:[]
}
```

Input is DOCX only and at most 10 MiB; there are no operation/path options. Reports have at most 50 source-table descriptors, 100 rows and 32 columns each, 20,000 aggregate rectangular slots and 256 KiB serialized output. Unsupported tables have both dimensions zero, null widths/signature and a nonempty reason. A positive shape with unavailable widths or signature also requires a disclosed reason. Notices and reasons are bounded inert strings, never markup.

The extractor computes table signatures from canonical source geometry plus normalized plain text. The editor must associate imported tables only through unique matching signatures; ordinals and a successful containment report do not authorize guessing a correspondence. No width should be applied to an ambiguous, mismatched or unsupported table.

This table grid is independent of merged-cell structure and is retained by recovery/version history and sanitized PDFix table copying. Widths represent proportions fitted to the available page/cell width, not an assertion that original absolute table size or Word pagination is retained.

# Email and clipboard creation coding — 2026-10-11

F54 and F55 add a reviewed creation dialog which hands editable content to the existing Document editor through `onCreateDocument({title, initialContent, importWarning})`. Page setup, text/image arrangement and reviewed PDF export use the existing document pipeline. The dialog closes and invokes `onClosed` before handing off content. This is coding evidence, not a release or UI certification.

## F54: bounded EML creation

The native `importEmailMessage()` entry selects one local `.eml`, retains an immutable source snapshot outside the renderer and invokes `email-message-read` in the contained document engine. `EmailMessageService` refuses missing snapshots, files over 10 MiB or fingerprint mismatches. There is no alternate uncontained parser. The returned report is checked for source hash, exact shape and bounded sizes before renderer handoff.

Supported MIME behavior:

- From, To, Cc, Bcc, Date, Subject, Reply-To and Message-ID; folded headers and RFC 2047 B/Q encoded words.
- Multipart boundaries, up to 200 MIME parts and 12 levels. `multipart/alternative` prefers available plain text. Other supported multipart bodies are combined with separators.
- 7bit, 8bit, binary, strict base64 and quoted-printable decoding. Header blocks are limited to 64 KiB each and 256 KiB overall; decoded aggregate content is limited to 10 MiB. Body parts and combined body are limited to 1 MiB.
- UTF-8, ASCII, ISO-8859-1/Latin-1 (decoded using the web-compatible Windows-1252 mapping), Windows-1252 and UTF-16LE/BE. Unsupported charset body parts are explicitly omitted with a warning; encoded headers retain literal text when decoding fails.
- Simple `filename`, `name` and nonsegmented RFC 2231 extended filename parameters. Encoded or unsupported extended names carry a warning; segmented filename parameters are not reconstructed.
- Text/plain and a small inert HTML formatting vocabulary. Source attributes, URLs, scripts, styles, links, tables, SVG and remote/inline images are stripped or simplified. No HTML source is executed and no remote image retrieval occurs. Image positions become visible omission markers. The editor applies its existing DOMPurify sanitizer again.

Every detected nonbody MIME part/attachment is listed with name, MIME type, decoded byte count when available and an explicit omission reason. Unknown decoded sizes are displayed as unavailable. Multipart attachments are inventoried as single omitted attachments; embedded `message/rfc822`, signed/encrypted bodies, calendar items and arbitrary file types are not opened or decoded recursively. All attachment bytes are omitted from the created document and PDF. Attachment preservation, extraction, embedded attachment PDF output and signature authenticity checks are not implemented in this route.

The created document contains supported headers/body plus the attachment inventory and omission reasons. It preserves editable content, not original email typography, CSS, tables, threading metadata or client-specific layout. Truncated/ambiguous MIME, malformed transfer encoding in a body and excessive resource use fail closed. Source path/content are not sent to network services.

## F55: explicit clipboard creation

`readCreationClipboard()` is invoked only by the Paste clipboard now button. It provides at most 1 MiB UTF-8 plain text and a static PNG image up to 5 MiB/4 million pixels. Text and image can be included in the same explicit paste. No polling or browser clipboard permission fallback is used. HTML, file references and other clipboard formats are omitted.

The dialog permits up to 20 items, editable text, image descriptions, reordering and removal. It shows decoded image dimensions and any pixel reduction notice. Images pass through the existing bounded image worker and become the existing `documentImage` inline PNG schema, with 512 KiB normalized assets, up to 20 images and 12 million aggregate pixels. Worker preparation can be canceled; failed preparation does not partially append clipboard items. Clipboard source bytes are cleared after image preparation. The arranged rich document is limited to 1.6 MB before handoff.

Review acknowledgement is reset when content/order changes. The next step opens the ordinary Document editor for further editing, image size/alignment, margins/orientation and export review. No automatic PDF saving occurs. This route does not retain clipboard file formats, rich clipboard styling, vector assets or floating image placement.

## Validation scope

Only one focused syntax/model check was requested for these additions. No application build, native contained process launch, Windows clipboard interaction, PDF export or broad UI sweep is claimed by this coding note. Native dialog snapshot/clipboard and app registration are owned by the main integration changes; the files here implement the contained MIME operation/service and review/handoff dialog.

# Contained native FDF comment exchange — October 9, 2026

Supported standard comment exchange is coded and integrated, not yet accepted against real Revu/Acrobat files. Import and export are available in the reader tools and command palette. This is a comment adapter; FDF form-value submission and full FDF compatibility remain unfinished.

Export uses the fixed contained source-comment inventory and at most 1,000 explicitly selected occurrences. The child maps supported Text, Line, Square, Circle, Polygon, PolyLine, Ink, Highlight, Underline, Squiggly and StrikeOut comments into actual FDF 1.2 indirect objects, classic xref/trailer and EOF, with Unicode hex literals. A separate bounded grammar readback compares each encoded annotation dictionary. The renderer shows actual output, individual result/omission receipts and source hashes before a native token-only exclusive save. Existing private fields, rich text and appearance payloads are not claimed preserved by this exchange.

Import reads a user-chosen regular FDF under 8 MiB through a native file picker, retains exact selected bytes and binds their hash to the chosen PDF. The child parser accepts a bounded inert FDF 1.2–1.7 single-revision object grammar, at most 1,000 comment dictionaries, 10,000 objects, 100,000 parsed nodes and depth 16. Streams, filters, active/resource containers, appearances, encryption and incremental revisions are refused. The parser accepts supported PDFDocEncoding/UTF-16BE literals. Target-file and ID claims are ignored and never retrieve or authenticate a document.

Understood dictionaries adapt to the existing preserving XFDF native import helper. The proposal lists supported and omitted records, geometry, claimed author/text/reply/state data and unmapped fields. At most 200 selected records are added per prepared copy. The child independently checks retained original PDF structures and added annotation receipts. The reader compares actual changed pages and verifies original/new annotation identities and geometry before saving; every changed page and all result pages require explicit review. Gray/RGB color quantization, unsupported border/style fields and private data omissions are disclosed. This is not a promise of identical custom Bluebeam appearances or provenance authentication.

Main-retained import/export seals have separate output kinds, source IDs, tokens, source fingerprints and output hashes. New selection, invalidation, cancel, source departure, renderer failure and shutdown invalidate relevant receipts. Cancellation and close await native discard/termination; cleanup failure keeps the workspace guarded and closes the unsafe service. Originals and existing output filenames are never overwritten. Imports use the fixed 12 MiB request envelope and ordinary exports 2 MiB; output/report/schema limits apply.

# F63 fingerprint workflow — October 12, 2026

Connected **Verify PDF fingerprint** to Workspaces and the command finder. A native picker selects the original; a streaming parent SHA-256 reader uses 1 MiB chunks without parsing or modifying PDF content. Progress, cancellation, expected-hash comparison, JSON receipt import, exclusive receipt export and clearing are connected. The receipt records file name, byte count, check time, digest and the last reviewed comparison when present. It omits absolute source paths and document text. The UI distinguishes byte equality from signer/author identity and future integrity.

The reader checks regular files, link aliases, named/descriptor identity, size and timestamps before/after reading, catches growth/short reads, and checks cancellation before publishing a result. An imported fingerprint is data, not an authenticated trust assertion. Exports use the existing new-copy exclusive writer and recheck the receipt after the save chooser. # F58 / R48 folder search coding — October 11, 2026

Status: coded expansion of selected-file search; partial target, not accepted or release-ready.

The existing search dialog now offers an explicit native **Choose PDF folder** action. The user reviews PDF-only selectable-text search, recursion (unchecked initially), and session-only access before the picker. The resulting dialog shows the selected absolute folder and scope. Search grants do not imply editing, watching, recipes or saved indexing. Clear search revokes access and removes match excerpts, file metadata and retained buffers; closing, renderer teardown and the existing expiry also revoke grants. No new persistent index or consent store is created. Persistence is deliberately unsupported and the IPC rejects other purposes, file types and persistence values.

Folder discovery returns a session token immediately and runs asynchronously. The renderer polls bounded metadata/progress, allows Stop, and retains the discovered subset when enumeration is canceled. Limits are 1,000 PDFs, 20,000 directory entries, 2,000 directories, 32 subfolder levels and two minutes. Files/errors within those bounds are returned, with explicit partial/skipped reports. Error details are capped at 500 rows; the skipped counter continues. Sequential search makes one independently checked snapshot at a time, retains at most one native PDF buffer, and releases it after extraction. No folder-wide PDF buffer or extracted-text cache is assembled. Match snippets and source fingerprints stay in memory until clear/close/expiry. Search snapshots can involve transient native allocation, IPC and parser copies; this is bounded per file, not a claim of a single physical byte copy.

The new fixed Windows attributes broker reads no PDF content. User paths are JSON stdin values, not PowerShell script interpolation. It uses GetFileAttributes to reject all reparse points (including junctions, links and cloud placeholders), offline and recall flags, and network drives. It fails closed when that broker is unavailable. All ancestors are checked, real paths must match lexical paths and remain inside the selected root, PDF hardlinks are rejected, and discovered file identity/size/timestamps are checked before and after snapshot reads. Changed, missing, inaccessible, excessive-size, protected, malformed and extraction-failed PDFs have visible reports. Originals are fingerprint-checked before opening a result. Strict rejection can exclude some synchronized folders even if their content is hydrated; it does not weaken containment to accommodate them.

Existing individual-file APIs remain compatible. Added native APIs are `selectFolder(path, options)`, `folderStatus(token)`, `cancelFolder(token)` and `release(token, id)`. Folder options are exactly `{recursive: boolean, purpose: 'search', persistence: 'session', fileTypes: ['pdf']}`. `bytes(token, id)` continues to return the existing payload for selected files and returns a promise for folder files. Folder discovery metadata has no hash until the first independently checked snapshot; the renderer verifies returned bytes against their SHA-256 before extraction. Existing native callers await the IPC result. A release during a folder read invalidates that read.

The existing PDF.js selected-text search path is reused with physical page references, permission/password handling, a 120-second per-file extraction deadline, 100 MB/500-page per-PDF bounds, 2,000 total matches, 32 MB total extracted text and 2 MB per extracted page/text segment. Scans need OCR; comments, metadata and attachments are omitted. A large folder can hit the combined text/match limit before every discovered PDF is searched. Opening a result uses the existing source-opening workspace handoff.

Remaining work and security limits:

- There is no persistent encrypted index, incremental reindexer, index export or independent history management. Every new query rereads/extracts selected folder PDFs; index deletion is represented by removing the session cache because no saved index exists.
- Existing search extraction uses PDF.js in the renderer's worker architecture. It is not the native AppContainer PDF service. This change introduces no new PDF parser, but it does not prove OS containment, worker memory ceilings or native sandbox parity for this existing path. Broader parser containment remains unresolved.
- Path ancestry/realpath/stat checks detect ordinary link and file replacement changes. They do not establish a native handle-relative, deny-delete directory lease. A hostile directory/reparse replacement between a check and a filesystem operation remains an acceptance gap, including the existing `FileStore.open` handoff. The feature must not be described as having proved race-free grant containment.
- PDFs over 100 MB or 500 pages are visibly skipped; disk-backed whole-folder large-PDF search and OCR indexing are not implemented.
- Stop returns after any outstanding filesystem/attributes request completes (attributes request timeout is ten seconds). Extraction cancellation terminates the current existing PDF.js task and cancels/releases the native per-file read. No directory watcher is installed.
- No hundreds-file throughput, hostile junction race, cloud-sync, cancellation, renderer teardown, memory-pressure, permission-restriction or packaged-Windows acceptance run was performed for this coding pass. Root integration/build is separate evidence.

Validation: native search modules and renderer module parsed successfully with Node's module parser. An initial ad hoc syntax harness incorrectly parsed `import.meta` as a script; the corrected module-parser harness passed. No broad test suite was added or run.

Here is the complete, categorized breakdown of everything where **Adobe Acrobat Pro beats PDFix**, based on Adobe’s actual enterprise capabilities and the explicit exclusions, deferrals, and gaps listed in the PDFix catalog:

---

### 1. Legal, Cryptographic & Enterprise Signatures
* **Certified PKI Signatures:** Adobe natively integrates with the **AATL (Adobe Approved Trust List)** and **EUTL (European Union Trust List)**. When you sign in Adobe with a hardware token, SmartCard, or digital certificate, the PDF is cryptographically sealed, tamper-evident, and legally recognized in court under ESIGN, UETA, and eIDAS.
  * *PDFix status:* **Explicitly excluded for initial release.** Only supports visual stamps and drawn/typed visual marks, which have zero cryptographic proof.
* **Cloud Signature Routing & Audit Trails (Adobe Sign):** Adobe offers multi-party signature workflows, automated routing orders, authentication challenges (SMS/email OTP), and legally binding audit logs.
  * *PDFix status:* **Excluded/deferred (F39).** No external signature dispatch, no recipient tracking, and no bulk signature/payment pipelines.

---

### 2. Print-Shop, Prepress & Color Management
* **Commercial Prepress & Preflight:** Adobe includes the industry-standard Preflight engine (Callas Software), capable of automated inspection, color-profile conversion, and syntax verification for commercial printers.
* **Color Trapping & Plate Separation Preview:** Adobe allows commercial printers to inspect individual CMYK and Pantone/spot color plates, overprint simulations, dot gain, and color trapping.
* **Print Standards (PDF/X):** Acrobat Pro can validate and enforce PDF/X-1a, PDF/X-3, PDF/X-4, and PDF/X-6 compliance.
  * *PDFix status:* **Explicitly excluded/deferred (M10.02, F40).** PDFix explicitly excludes advanced print-shop color management/trapping and has deferred PDF/X verification.

---

### 3. Standards Compliance & Archival (PDF/A, PDF/E)
* **Turnkey Archival Conversion (PDF/A):** Adobe can analyze arbitrary PDFs and convert them into compliant ISO standards (PDF/A-1b, PDF/A-2b, PDF/A-3u) with embedded ICC profiles, device-independent colors, and embedded font subsets.
  * *PDFix status:* **Deferred (M10.01, F40).** PDFix treats standards compliance as a future candidate and explicitly notes that neither a visual match nor a file extension guarantees standard compliance.

---

### 4. Accessibility Remediation (Section 508 / PDF/UA / WCAG)
* **Industrial Tag Tree Editing:** Adobe Acrobat Pro contains a full Tag Tree Editor, Reading Order Panel, and Touch Up Reading Order tools required to make PDFs legally compliant for blind/low-vision users.
* **Automated Accessibility Auditing:** Adobe generates detailed compliance reports for PDF/UA and Section 508, allowing bulk artifact tagging, alt-text assignment, and table header mapping.
  * *PDFix status:* **Basic only (M08.01–02, F30).** PDFix only offers basic structural inspection and limited guided repairs; it lacks a full tag-tree remediation environment.

---

### 5. Advanced Forms & Dynamic Scripting
* **Dynamic XFA Forms:** Adobe supports complex, reflowing XML Forms Architecture (XFA) used by federal governments, defense agencies, and healthcare providers.
* **Embedded Acrobat JavaScript Engine:** Adobe executes rich JavaScript inside forms for live validation, arithmetic recalculations, button actions, and formatting.
* **2D Barcode Fields:** Acrobat dynamically generates paper 2D barcodes that encode filled form data as the user types.
* **Database & Web Submissions:** Adobe forms can submit payloads directly to web endpoints or corporate databases.
  * *PDFix status:* **Hard exclusion (M04.01–03, M10.02).** PDFix **refuses to run PDF scripts/macros** for security, does not support XFA forms, and excludes barcode fields entirely.

---

### 6. PDF Portfolios & Container Formats
* **Multi-File PDF Portfolios:** Adobe can bundle dozens of different files (Word, Excel, CAD, video, other PDFs) inside an interactive, navigable 3D or grid-based portfolio package.
  * *PDFix status:* **Explicitly excluded (M10.02).** PDFix cannot create or navigate PDF portfolios.

---

### 7. 3D Models, Geospatial Maps & Multimedia
* **Interactive 3D PDF:** Adobe natively renders embedded 3D CAD models (U3D and PRC formats), allowing users to rotate parts, create cross-section slices, measure 3D geometries, and toggle part assemblies.
* **Geospatial PDF (GIS):** Acrobat recognizes embedded coordinate metadata (latitude/longitude) and allows GIS measurements.
* **Embedded Multimedia:** Acrobat plays embedded audio, video, and rich interactive media.
  * *PDFix status:* **Explicitly excluded (M10.02).** PDFix excludes 3D models, geospatial measurements, and embedded media playback.

---

### 8. Enterprise Rights Management (DRM) & Policy Control
* **Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) Document Security:** Organizations can enforce central DRM policies—revoking access to a document remotely even after it has been downloaded, expiring access on specific dates, or restricting printing.
  * *PDFix status:* **Explicitly excluded (M10.02).** Only supports basic local password encryption (open/permission passwords); zero enterprise DRM support.

---

### 9. Multi-Platform Ecosystem & Browser Sharing
* **Cloud Link Reviews (No Software Required):** Adobe allows you to generate a web link where anyone on a Mac, Chromebook, phone, or PC can comment on a PDF in a web browser without installing anything.
* **Mobile Ecosystem & "Liquid Mode":** Adobe has mature iOS/Android apps with reflowing "Liquid Mode" for reading documents on phones.
  * *PDFix status:* **Windows desktop only (F36).** Built strictly for Windows; browser-based shared review and cloud links are deferred candidates.

---

### 10. Engine Maturity on Corrupted/Wild PDFs
* **30 Years of Real-World Parser Tolerances:** Acrobat can reliably open broken, malformed, 1990s PostScript-derived, or non-spec PDFs produced by hundreds of different third-party generators without crashing.
  * *PDFix status:* **Under active development.** A large corpus of adversarial and broken files has not yet been accepted or certified through runtime release gates (F42).
