8. Scanned paper forms: detect likely fields and help users place text and checkmarks even when a form has no interactive fields.
9. Form behavior: preserve field values, calculate fields when supported, show required unanswered fields, and keep tab order usable. Clearly identify forms the app cannot safely fill.
10. Different kinds of signatures: distinguish a typed or drawn signature from a certificate-based digital signature. Show whether an existing signature validates, and warn if an edit may affect it.
11. Annotations: preserve comments and highlights when saving or converting. Let users hide, show, print, flatten, or export annotations without confusing them with the document’s original content.
Editing, conversion, and document fidelity
12. Compare more than text: compare page order, text, images, and scanned pages; let users review changes side by side. Scanned pages may need visual comparison as well as text comparison.
13. Conversion choices: let users choose what to preserve—links, images, page size, bookmarks, or form fields—and explain when those things may not survive conversion.
14. Images from Apple devices: account for HEIC/HEIF orientation and metadata. For a Live Photo, identify whether the still image and motion clip are both present, and let users export them separately.
15. Document standards: consider optional PDF/A output for long-term archiving and an accessibility check for tagged PDFs. Accessible PDFs rely on structure such as tags and reading order; visual appearance alone doesn’t provide that structure.
16. Safe file extraction: if PDFix supports ZIP or embedded files, show what’s inside and ask before extracting. Never run extracted files automatically.
AI, privacy, and recovery
17. AI that can see page layout: some questions depend on charts, diagrams, or page images, not just extracted text. Show whether the selected model can read images, and label answers based on OCR as uncertain when recognition is weak.
18. Safe AI handling: treat instructions inside a document as document content, not commands for the agent. Keep AI in read-only mode unless the user approves a specific change.
19. Privacy cleanup: let users clear recent-file history, remove temporary files, and see whether any data was sent to an online provider. Avoid putting document text in diagnostic logs.
20. Recoverable operations: save before risky changes, keep a recoverable original, and clearly distinguish “rotate this view” from “rotate and save these pages.”
21. Bad conversion recovery: let users compare the converted copy with the source and discard the output without losing the original.
22. Duplicate files: warn gently when the user may be saving a second copy with the same name, and offer clear choices such as replace, keep both, or choose another folder.
For the requirements Codex is working from, I’d add these first: bookmarks and page views, OCR cleanup and review, safe form/signature handling, preservation of annotations and document structure, visual comparison, and recovery of originals. The rest can go into later phases after the core app works.

# PDFix Missing Features — Master Gap List

This consolidates the useful missing-feature ideas discussed for PDFix. It is a planning list, not a claim that these features are implemented. The goal is a simple document workspace with useful PDF, document, photo, and engineering drawing tools—not a copy of every professional publishing suite.

## Status note

The Drive project documents working PDF reading, page organization, crop/resize, markups, supported forms and visual signatures, OCR, image-to-PDF, comparison, and local recovery. The README and architecture describe page-range selection and automatic splitting as implemented, while the older feature tracker still lists automatic splitting as future work. Confirm that tracker status against the current build.

## 1. PDF security, cleanup, and protection

- **Verified permanent redaction:** remove selected text, regions, image content, and underlying objects so hidden information cannot be recovered. Search repeated words/numbers, show every match, and require review before applying.
- **Sanitize before sharing:** inspect and selectively remove metadata, embedded attachments, hidden layers, comments, form values, scripts/actions, and other hidden content. Show what will be removed.
- **Password protection and changes:** add or change PDF passwords using a reviewed implementation; explain permissions and never bypass access controls.
- **Digital signature validation:** detect certificate signatures and report valid, invalid, or unable to verify only when a reviewed validator supports the result. Warn when edits may invalidate signatures.
- **Separate signature types:** distinguish visual signatures, certificate-based signatures, and external signature requests.
- **Safe links and attachments:** show external destinations before opening; list attachments with type/size details and save only to a chosen location. Never execute PDF scripts or auto-open extracted files.
- **Plain-language security report:** explain encryption, signatures, active content, attachments, and unsupported structures.

## 2. Compression, conversion, and PDF creation

- **Compression with quality preview:** show expected size savings and let users inspect quality before saving. Disclose possible loss of text, forms, links, annotations, or other structures.
- **Broader conversions:** support more tested conversions between PDFs, documents, images, and data files. For each, disclose what happens to fonts, page breaks, images, links, bookmarks, forms, and annotations.
- **Multiple images to PDF:** add an ordered image list, per-image rotation, page layout, paper size, and recoverable source references. Current documented workflow makes one PDF from one image.
- **Create PDFs from text/documents:** provide page size, margins, fonts, page breaks, and preview.
- **More export options:** save a page or selected pages as images; export selected pages as separate PDFs; consider reverse PDF-to-image conversion.
- **Page additions:** insert blank pages, replace pages with corrected scans, and add page numbers, headers, footers, watermarks, or reusable Draft/Approved/Reviewed stamps.
- **Metadata tools:** inspect and optionally edit or remove title, author, subject, keywords, and other supported metadata.
- **Output naming:** offer clear names, keep-both, and destination choices; never silently overwrite originals or unrelated files.

## 3. Paper, print, engineering, and architecture drawings

- **Paper-size presets:** common US Letter and Legal, engineering ANSI A–E, architectural ARCH A–E, and ISO A-series such as A0–A4, where supported by the operation.
- **More page views:** single page, continuous scroll, facing pages, two-page spread, and side-by-side pages, with clear page order.
- **Large-sheet navigation:** smooth pan and zoom, zoom-to-region, fit-sheet, and return-to-previous-view for blueprints, plans, schematics, and maps.
- **Scale-aware measurement:** calibrate drawing scale first, then measure distance, perimeter, and area with visible units and a way to confirm calibration.
- **Drawing markups:** dimension lines, arrows, callouts, revision clouds, and color-coded comments alongside notes, highlights, and drawing tools.
- **PDF layers:** show or hide layers where the PDF contains them.
- **Drawing revision comparison:** align sheets and compare with a transparent overlay or side-by-side view; allow alignment adjustment when scale or position shifted.
- **Large-format printing:** print at actual size, fit to a chosen sheet, or tile across pages with overlap and alignment marks. Include ranges, orientation, scaling, and multiple pages per sheet.
- **Booklet printing:** provide layout preview and clear paper/duplex requirements.
- **Sheet sets:** group related drawings, navigate sheets, and preserve order.
- **Drawing information:** show sheet number, title, revision, dimensions, and page size when present.
- **CAD boundary:** do not imply PDFix edits CAD models; DWG and other CAD formats need separate decoder, licensing, and corpus evaluation.

## 4. Forms, signatures, and review

- **Create basic fillable forms:** add supported text, checkbox, radio, and choice fields, in addition to filling existing fields.
- **Improve form usability:** clearer labels, tab order, required-field guidance, supported fonts, and explanations for unsupported calculations/fields.
- **Form submission:** save a completed copy, print it, or export supported field data; explain unsupported fields.
- **Signature placement help:** identify likely signature/date/initial fields and suggest locations, but require confirmation of content and placement.
- **Reusable assets:** save user-approved signatures, initials, stamps, and common markups with clear local storage and deletion controls.
- **Broader annotations:** edit third-party annotations, threaded replies, and comment exchange only after preservation tests.
- **Annotation export:** offer a separate annotation summary or copy where verifiable.

## 5. Scanning, OCR, and information extraction

- **Scan from a device:** import from scanner/document camera, including multi-page scans where supported; preview, reorder, rotate, or remove pages before making a PDF.
- **Scan cleanup:** preview deskew, contrast/brightness cleanup, rotation, and proposed blank-page removal. Distinguish faint content from blank pages and allow undo.
- **Broader OCR:** add only tested bundled/installed languages; make language choice clear and show confidence as an estimate.
- **Uncertainty review:** locate uncertain words/lines on the scan, preserve page references, and require review before saving corrections.
- **Extract tables:** offer table-to-CSV/spreadsheet export only when recognition is suitable, with preview to catch misaligned rows and columns.
- **Searchable documents:** preserve scan images and explain when OCR reading order or recognition needs review.
- **Clear scan limits:** explain limits for handwriting, low resolution, skew, mixed languages, and complex reading order.

## 6. File formats, photos, and editing fidelity

Evaluate and add tested support for HEIC/HEIF (orientation and metadata choices), multipage TIFF, RTF, XLSX/PPTX preview/conversion, legacy DOC/XLS/PPT, and Apple Pages/Numbers/Keynote. Add a meaningful Markdown preview and structured table views for CSV/data files while retaining source editing. Complete real-file fixtures for XML, YAML, CSV, BMP, and uncommon image variants before claiming support. Clearly separate Open, Preview, Edit, and Convert for each format. Explain fidelity limits before conversion. Let users choose whether photo metadata/color profiles are kept or removed.

## 7. Navigation, search, and multi-file workflows

- **Search navigation:** match counts and next/previous controls.
- **Search selected files:** search only deliberately selected files; show filename and page for each result.
- **Quick action finder:** “What do you want to do?” search for sign, split, compress, OCR, compare, or convert.
- **Move pages across PDFs:** drag pages between open PDFs with a visible preview.
- **Page navigation:** jump by printed page label; edit bookmarks/table-of-contents entries; safely show internal link destinations.
- **Batch operations:** queue supported conversion, compression, rename, combine, and other verified actions with per-file progress/results, cancellation, output location, collision handling, and bounded resources.
- **Reusable workflows:** repeat reviewed sequences such as OCR → review → save copy or combine → number pages → print; show and allow editing of steps before running.
- **Recover interrupted jobs:** let users retry/discard failed or canceled jobs without confusing partial output for completed work.
- Search and batch features must not imply broad folder scanning.

## 8. Accessibility, quality checks, and inspection

- **Accessibility checks:** inspect tags, reading order, headings, links, and form labels; distinguish searchable OCR from accessible structure.
- **Guided accessibility repair:** offer fixes only when results can be validated; don’t promise automatic tagging makes a PDF fully accessible.
- **Document health report:** identify missing fonts, oversized images, broken links, unusual page sizes, unsupported features, and possible print problems; offer safe fixes only where verified.
- **Trustworthy file details:** show page dimensions/orientation/count, file size, text searchability, encryption state, and feature limits.
- **Accessible job status:** announce progress, failures, and cancellation to keyboard and screen-reader users.
- **Scalable interface:** test larger text, contrast, visible focus, keyboard navigation, and reduced motion throughout dialogs/workflows.
- **Print preview:** inspect prepared output, selected pages, paper, orientation, scaling, annotations, and rasterization before Windows handoff.
- Physical printer validation remains a release check; simulated preparation alone does not prove paper output.

## 9. Privacy, sharing, Windows, and AI

- **Share local copies:** provide Windows share handoff for a new copy. For cloud links/uploads, show service, account, destination, and permissions before sending.
- **Transfer history:** if online AI/sharing is added, show what files were sent, to which endpoint/service, and when; allow cleanup.
- **Optional AI providers/agents:** scope each request to selected files; show provider, model, endpoint, destination, and possible account charges before transfer.
- **Cited answers:** provide page/line references where available and distinguish source text from generated explanation.
- **Read-only AI by default:** treat document contents as untrusted; prevent automatic saving/exporting/overwriting/tool use. Require separate approval and a reviewable result for changes.
- **Connection controls:** test, select, and remove connections; store secrets using Windows-backed secure storage and fail closed if unavailable.
- **Hermes:** evaluate its documented HTTP API before implementing.
- **Harness:** defer until the exact product/interface is identified.
- **Windows lifecycle:** installer, uninstaller, updates, optional file associations, and Open with PDFix.
- **Release readiness:** security, licensing, dependency/SBOM, performance, clean-machine install, and real-file corpus reviews.

## 10. Later candidates and first-release boundaries

Later candidates: online signature requests/tracking, shared/cloud review, online form response collection, PDF/A or PDF/X validation, tagged-PDF validation, accessibility repair, and Bates numbering. Each needs a clear user need and reviewed engine/service before it appears as working.

Keep bulk signature/payment workflows, PDF portfolios, barcode fields, advanced print-shop color/trapping, geospatial/3D measurement, embedded multimedia, presentation generation, and CAD model editing out of the initial scope unless the direction changes.

## Current product features (not missing)

The project documents a Windows-first local Electron workspace; picker and drag/drop; recents/favorites; PDF reading, search, selection, print preparation, outlines and saved reading positions; page organization, crop/resize, page ranges and documented automatic splitting; PDF comparison; PDFix markups; supported AcroForm filling and confirmed visual signatures; local English OCR with review; basic DOCX/TXT/source editing; version/recovery tools; and one-image-to-one-page PDF creation. Each has limits; some support applies only to tested subsets.

# Large PDF native loading

Implemented in `desktop/file-store.cjs` and `desktop/large-pdf-store.cjs`.

- The existing byte-packet path remains for sources at or below 100 MiB. Non-PDF opening, native editing/conversion, and output validation retain their 100 MiB limits. An explicit `open(..., {maxBytes})` remains a hard opening cap.
- Default PDF opening above 100 MiB attempts a disk snapshot up to the current 1 GiB viewer resource ceiling. Failure messages identify the viewer budget, RAM shortage, disk shortage, changed input, invalid header, or inaccessible storage. They do not describe the large-PDF reading ceiling as a 100 MB limit.
- RAM admission estimates `3 * PDF length + 256 MiB` for viewer work and leaves another 512 MiB for the operating system. The required available-memory threshold is therefore `3 * PDF length + 768 MiB`, compared with `os.freemem()` at admission. This estimate cannot guarantee successful rendering of complex PDFs.
- The bundled PDF.js range viewer still reserves a full-length byte array. Native range loading removes full-file native/IPC copies; it does **not** make total viewer RAM independent of document length.
- Where `fs.statfs` is supported, disk admission requires PDF length plus 64 MiB of headroom on the application-folder volume. Unsupported filesystem-statistics platforms still get bounded copying and a disk/permissions explanation on failure.
- A held original descriptor is copied and SHA-256 hashed sequentially using a 256 KiB buffer into an exclusive, random file in an app-owned temporary directory. Only the first 1,024 bytes are sniffed for `%PDF-`; no PDF parser or engine runs in this native path. Source descriptor size/device/inode/modified/changed times are fenced before and after copying, and an extra-byte probe rejects growth.
- The completed snapshot is made read-only, reopened read-only, and retained behind the opaque source ID. Snapshot paths and descriptors never appear in range IPC. Successful opening returns metadata with `rangeSource: {length, chunkSize: 262144}`, `largeFile: true`, a slower-reading notice, and reading-only capability metadata.
- `readPdfRange(id, begin, end)` accepts only safe integer, nonempty, in-bounds ranges of at most 1 MiB. It reads the retained snapshot descriptor exactly and fences both descriptor and snapshot-path metadata before and after the read. Missing, replaced, mutated, or ended snapshots cannot continue serving ranges.
- File-backed sources preserve metadata, fingerprint, reading-position, and source-check access. Their `bytes` getter throws `FileError` with `LARGE_PDF_OPERATION` and explains the existing 100 MiB per-operation editing/export limit. Copy and split saving also reject file-backed sources.
- Opening, reading ranges, releasing, clearing, and disposal use one serialized session queue. Retained sessions are capped at ten; their in-memory source bytes remain capped at 100 MiB, excluding disk snapshots. Normal opening clears prior sources only when the replacement is ready.
- `release(id)` closes and unlinks only the app-owned snapshot associated with that ID. `clearSessions()` immediately invalidates the open generation, then serializes cleanup while leaving the store usable by a replacement renderer. Snapshot copying checks cancellation between chunks. `dispose()` invalidates the generation permanently and closes/removes all tracked snapshots. Failed-open temporary files are removed; failed removals remain privately tracked for disposal retry and yield explicit cleanup errors. Abrupt OS/process termination cannot execute asynchronous disposal.
- Each snapshot root has an immutable, synced `snapshot-owner.json` marker containing exactly the application owner, version, UUID, and matching root leaf. The marker is durable before any UUID PDF file is created; it never needs a mutable file-list update that could be torn by process termination. The current store tracks exact owned UUID file leaves privately. On startup, `LargePdfStore.init()` scans only immediate matching roots, skips the active store root, reads ownership markers with a 16 KiB bound and descriptor/path stat fences, and derives a list of at most 128 regular UUID PDF leaves. Roots containing unrecognized leaves, links, or invalid markers are left untouched. Known cleanup revalidates root, marker, and leaf identity before each exact unlink, then removes the marker and empty directory; it never deletes recursively. Cleanup failure or invalid/torn marker warnings are exposed through `snapshotCleanupWarning` and the existing `recoveryWarning` without interrupting recent-file history loading. The application must hold its single-instance lock before initializing this cleanup.
- A trusted optional `store.onOpenProgress(event)` callback receives `{stage, name, size, bytes, total}` for large opening. Stages are `preparing`, `progress` (approximately every 500 ms while copying), `done` after the session commits, and `canceled` when opening fails or is invalidated. Callback exceptions and promise rejections are ignored; progress never reveals native snapshot paths or descriptors.

1. `desktop/file-store.cjs` accepts a user-selected regular file, checks its type and tracks its source identity. PDFs above the ordinary 100 MiB tool/input limit enter `LargePdfStore`; ordinary PDFs can also switch to paged viewing when their page count exceeds 500.

This is not unlimited-size support or a guarantee of smooth rendering. The current viewer admits up to 1 GiB per PDF and 500 pages, subject to available resources. The installed PDF.js worker reserves a full-length byte array even when using ranges. On-demand reading avoids extra full-file copies and eager reads; total memory is not constant. # Source-backed drawing-wide comment inventory

The review service now has a distinct read-only source-file path for opened PDFs
larger than 100 MiB and no larger than 256 MiB. The user's approximately
156,000 KB drawing fits that byte admission limit. Admission is not a guarantee
that its object complexity fits the isolated parser's memory or traversal budgets.
The reader continues to admit PDFs up to 1 GiB; inventory above 256 MiB remains an
implementation gap and produces an explicit limit message before staging.

## Main-process source contract

`FileStore` adds a non-enumerable `reviewInput()` capability to each file-backed
source. The renderer receives only the existing opaque session ID and safe open
metadata, now including `sourceSha256` and `capabilities.reviewInventory`.
It never receives the capability, a snapshot path, or a native descriptor.

`reviewInput()` returns a frozen `{length, sha256, stage, validate}` object.
`stage(target, {signal})` exclusively creates the contained job's `input.bin` and
copies from the already-retained immutable snapshot descriptor in 256 KiB chunks.
The parent never allocates or transmits a whole-source byte array for this route.
The copy hashes exactly the staged bytes and verifies the opened fingerprint,
retained descriptor stat, path stat, session ID, and FileStore generation.
Staging has a 120-second deadline, abort checks between reads and writes, and a
disk admission check for the source length plus 64 MiB when statfs is available.

Snapshot release invalidates capabilities immediately and waits for outstanding
staging leases before closing its descriptor or removing its owned leaf. A child
uses a separate contained staging copy, so no snapshot descriptor is inherited.
`validate()` must run before staging/launch and after child termination, before
returning a source-bound report. Session release during parsing invalidates that
result even if the contained parser completed successfully. Failed staging files
are left to the contained job owner's checked cleanup path.

## Contained operation and results

`PdfReviewService.inspect()` routes file-backed sources through
`_runContainedSourceFile(sourceId, null, 'review-inventory-file', input,
{pages}, validator)`. The distinct operation must be the only allowlisted
source-file operation in the shared containment service. It must require a
value-only result and an empty binary output. Paths or callbacks cannot appear
in renderer requests or the serialized child options.

The fixed child operation calls `inspectReviewSourceFile(bytes, pages)` after
bounded file input and source-hash validation. Only this entry point admits
256 MiB. Existing `inspectReview(bytes, pages, retainDocument)` remains capped
at 100 MiB, including callers that retain a document for editing or export.
Structural review extraction and its strict source-bound report validator are
shared, preserving physical page/object identities, reply relationships,
plain literal comments, flags, standard color metadata, and reported omissions.

Existing budgets remain: 500 pages, 10,000 annotations including popups,
100,000 indirect objects, 300,000 traversal nodes, bounded annotation strings,
and an 8 MiB complete inventory. All source pages are scanned for reply identity,
even when only selected-page literal fields are returned. A structural, source,
output, decoding, memory, or wall-clock failure returns an error without a partial
inventory. Read-only admission does not decode appearance streams, execute PDF
actions, or validate proprietary Bluebeam semantics or certificate trust.

## Reader integration and current limits

The review panel verifies large-file reports against the native open fingerprint
instead of reading or hashing `file.bytes`. It preserves search, filters, saved
filter sets, annotation details, source thread navigation, and bounds navigation.
Large-file edit actions and TXT/CSV/JSON/XFDF import/export actions remain disabled,
with method-level guards in addition to disabled controls. PDF copy permission
still controls access to the inventory.

# Multilingual OCR status

PDFix bundles local Tesseract 4.0.0 best-int language data from the official
`@tesseract.js-data/*` packages. The available printed-text choices are English
(`eng`), Spanish (`spa`), French (`fra`), German (`deu`), Portuguese (`por`),
and Italian (`ita`). Each run uses one language chosen by the user. The current
workflow does not guess a language or run an unselected language combination.

The recognition input stays local. Worker initialization receives the selected
code and loads its matching bundled `*.traineddata.gz`; the session and each
recognized page retain that code and `user-selected` source. TXT/CSV exports
include OCR language provenance. No online language download or handwriting
accuracy claim is part of this workflow.

Searchable PDF creation currently uses pdf-lib's standard Helvetica font. Its
encoding boundary is checked for every reviewed line, and the operation stops
with an actionable message if that font cannot encode a character. This is a
practical Western-script boundary; it does not claim reliable searchable output
for arbitrary Unicode scripts. TXT, CSV, and document-editor export preserve
Unicode text.

The official npm metadata labels each language package MIT, while the upstream
Tesseract `tessdata_best` training-data repository publishes its files under
Apache-2.0. Both notices are included with the copied runtime to preserve the
package metadata and upstream data terms. Tesseract.js and its WebAssembly core
license files are copied beside the bundled runtime. `scripts/copy-ocr-assets.mjs`
records package/version/license details in `dist/ocr-assets/languages.json`;
The Vite close-bundle hook now invokes this script; the six languages were included in the October 8 compilation milestone.

This is an incremental implementation. Current gaps include RTL and CJK
searchable PDF fonts, language detection, mixed-language pages, OCR recovery
across app restarts, orientation correction, handwriting support, and accuracy
benchmarks. The recognized-language choice is kept with the active OCR session
and output records, but those records are not persisted for crash recovery.

# PDFix original PDF editing fidelity — saved implementation

Updated 2026-10-04. This records code that is saved, not completed runtime acceptance.

## Embedded source-font text editing

The original-text editor now understands a bounded subset of embedded-font `ToUnicode` CMaps. This removes the previous blanket exclusion of PDFs whose original text uses embedded fonts, including many ordinary downloaded and Word-exported PDFs.

Supported source font shapes:

- Embedded simple `Type1` and `TrueType` fonts with one-byte declarative `ToUnicode` maps.
- Embedded `Type0` fonts using horizontal `Identity-H`, exactly one `CIDFontType0` or `CIDFontType2` descendant and a two-byte declarative `ToUnicode` map.
- Existing unembedded standard Type1 Western-font support remains available.
- `beginbfchar`, direct `beginbfrange`, array `beginbfrange`, fixed-width codespaces, valid BMP scalars and valid UTF-16 surrogate pairs.
- Individual string operands inside multipart `TJ` arrays. Original numeric spacing adjustments and the rest of each array remain byte-for-byte unchanged in the decoded content stream.

Replacement text reuses the original source font resource, size and character-code bytes. It does not paint over old text or substitute a visually similar font. A character must already have been decoded in a supported string using that same source font. When several source codes map to the same character, the current run's original code takes precedence; an ambiguous character absent from that run is refused. New glyphs are not synthesized. A missing, ambiguous or unavailable character prevents preview construction with a concrete explanation.

Ligatures and other mappings to multiple Unicode characters stay unmapped. Their affected strings are ineligible; supported mappings and other strings in the same font remain usable. This slice does not implement text shaping, bidirectional layout, paragraph reflow or font-file modification. A mapped character is not a guarantee that arbitrary rearrangements of complex-script glyphs will preserve shaping. The user must review the output layout.

The font name and observed-character count appear in the editor. Replacement runs retain original stable page/stream/byte-offset identities, so existing recovery and undo formats need no migration or new IPC route.

## Preservation and bounds

The replacement stream starts with a clone of the original stream dictionary. Its compression filter, decode parameters and derived length are replaced as required for the new payload; other dictionary fields remain. Only selected string token spans change. Shared original content-stream objects remain retained, and only the selected page's content reference points to the new stream. External-file content streams are refused.

Before changing text, the writer fingerprints each selected source font and its complete referenced object graph, including font descriptors, mappings and encoded font-program bytes. After saving and reopening the output, the same page font resource must produce the same SHA-256 proof. Stream `Length` is excluded as a writer-derived field, while actual encoded bytes, dictionary keys, references and values remain part of the proof. A changed or missing source font refuses the output.

Bounds include 1 MiB per decoded CMap, 8 MiB aggregate CMap bytes, 200 source fonts, 16,384 mappings per font, 65,536 usable mappings across fonts, 64 codespace ranges, 200,000 lexical tokens per CMap and bounded range expansion. Existing content-stream limits remain 8 MiB each, 64 MiB aggregate, 2,000 candidate strings and 200 staged text changes. Font preservation graphs are capped at 20,000 nodes, depth 32, 2,000 references and 100 MiB of encoded streams per proof. Existing 100 MiB / 500-page source and page geometry limits remain enforced.

Encrypted/protected, certified, digitally signed and dynamic XFA sources continue to be refused by the content writer. Originals are unchanged; editing saves a new reviewed copy. Replaced original streams remain in the PDF object graph, so this is editing and is not a permanent redaction operation.

# Original embedded-font glyph expansion

Saved October 7, 2026. Adopted F10 original-text editing expansion is coded; runtime/corpus acceptance remains deferred.

Previously, supported embedded fonts could only reuse characters already observed in editable source text. Replacement encoding now also accepts independently proven existing characters that have not yet appeared in those runs. This is a real extension of original text replacement: it changes the original supported content operand using the original font/code/size, not repainting, overlay text, substitution, font injection or redaction.

The new path applies to horizontal Type0/Identity-H fonts with one CIDFontType2 descendant, an embedded FontFile2 single TrueType `glyf` program, and an already declared bounded ToUnicode code mapping. Prefixed subset font names are refused. Absence of a subset prefix is not a certification that the font is a complete upstream font; every newly authorized character still needs its actual glyph/outline/metrics proof. Original observed-glyph editing remains available if expansion fails or is unsupported.

For each candidate existing code, the helper independently checks that the declared scalar Unicode value maps to the same nonzero GID through the embedded Unicode `cmap` (formats 4/12, Unicode or Windows Unicode records) and the PDF CIDToGIDMap (explicit mapping or Identity/default Identity). Conflicting Unicode maps, missing or out-of-range GIDs and ambiguous code choices refuse that expansion. TrueType `head`, `maxp`, `hhea`, `hmtx`, `loca` and `glyf` bounds/geometry are checked. Horizontal advance must agree with PDF `W`/`DW` to within 0.5 units per 1,000, allowing the PDF integer rounding of an otherwise proven metric. New codes must have positive advance and a valid complete simple outline, or an actual blank outline for Unicode space characters.

Simple outline checks cover contour endpoints, instruction-byte bounds, repeated flags, coordinate encodings/deltas, point bounds and small zero padding. Each GID outline is parsed once per font. Compound glyphs are currently refused for new-character expansion. Unicode marks/controls/formatting, contextual scripts, shaping, arbitrary text reflow, vertical writing, CFF, variable, SVG, color and bitmap font programs remain unsupported. The accepted scalar scripts are Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Common, Han, Hiragana and Katakana; this does not imply linguistic shaping or semantic layout support.

No source font dictionary, ToUnicode stream, CIDToGID mapping, font program, widths, resources or other text run is modified. The existing `originalFontProof` fingerprint still verifies the exact original dictionary/reference/stream graph before and after save. Encoding prefers a code already present in the edited run, otherwise a unique observed code, otherwise a unique independently proven existing code. Ambiguous alternatives refuse instead of guessing. Existing source-page/nested-Form paths, operand-span replacement, spacing numbers, source hashes and final output review remain in use.

This deliberately does **not** allocate codes for a Unicode character absent from the original ToUnicode map, extend CIDToGID/W, embed new outlines, rewrite font programs or update font resources. That broader capability needs an explicit allowed-font-object-change preservation contract, source/output glyph mapping verification and a writer that can preserve every original code/resource alongside new entries. Current save acceptance requires the entire original font object graph unchanged; silently weakening that proof would be incorrect.

# PDF source range queue repair

## Cause and primary source evidence

The previous renderer transport rejected its 65th queued request even though queued requests held only two offsets, not PDF byte buffers. A valid PDF.js burst could therefore abort a readable large PDF before the byte or native I/O budgets were reached.

The installed primary implementation is `pdfjs-dist` 6.3.289:

- `node_modules/pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker.mjs`, `ChunkedStreamManager._requestChunks`: `_requestsByChunk` admits each missing 256 KiB source chunk only once while pending, then `groupChunks` combines contiguous chunks into native range-reader requests.
- `node_modules/pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.mjs`, `PDFDataTransportStream.#onReceiveData`: responses are routed by their original `begin` offset. `PDFDataTransportStreamRangeReader._enqueue` completes and unregisters that reader synchronously after receiving one buffer.
- `PDFDataRangeTransport.onDataRange` calls its listener synchronously. `transport_stream_getArrayBuffer` copies partial typed-array views, so merged reads must deliver independent complete buffers rather than fragments or views into a larger assembly.
- `desktop/large-pdf-store.cjs` admits sources up to 1 GiB and serves native reads up to 1 MiB.

## Implemented algorithm

1. Bound all pending request records, including those in the active batch, by `ceil(source length / 256 KiB)`. The maximum is 4096 for the admitted 1 GiB source. A normal burst above 64 requests is queued instead of aborted. The source descriptor is checked against the existing 1 GiB admission ceiling.
2. Queue offset metadata only. One drain controls byte allocation and native I/O; requests wait behind its active assembly.
3. Start from the oldest request and scan queued records in arrival order. Coalesce overlapping or adjacent requests only when their union is at most 1 MiB, and never read a gap or assemble a whole source through merging. Larger original requests retain their single original assembly, up to the existing 64 MiB limit.
4. Read each batch through the admitted hardware profile's validated concurrency of one to four native calls (default four), each at most 1 MiB. Fully covered small requests that arrive during the read reuse the completed batch's bytes. Overlapping small requests therefore reuse disk reads where safe.
5. Deliver exactly one complete response per original range reader. A merged batch uses exact independent `bytes.slice` buffers, each at most 1 MiB. An unmerged original range transfers its assembly directly. An older queued request excluded from a batch blocks later requests with the same `begin` from joining that batch, preserving PDF.js's begin-only routing order.
6. Validate response types and exact lengths. Failure aborts the generation and clears pending metadata before calling the existing loading-task error handler. Every asynchronous native read is covered by `Promise.all`; aborted or obsolete generations neither copy nor deliver responses. The fire-and-forget drain catches failures, and asynchronous error-handler failures remain handled.

## Limits and remaining scope

The original refusal for a whole-source request or an individual request larger than 64 MiB remains. This patch does not add eager full reads, increase native read sizes, or raise the source ceiling. A request count beyond the source-derived metadata invariant still fails explicitly; it is outside the installed worker's deduplicated request behavior.

The transport controls one active assembly (at most 64 MiB), at most four outstanding 1 MiB native responses, and small exact response copies from a merged assembly of at most 1 MiB. PDF.js retains its own source and decoded data, and delivered buffers can outlive the transport operation. These transport limits are not a claim of constant application RAM usage.

# Size-based PDF splitting — F05

Saved source implements a real maximum encoded file-size rule alongside every-N, custom ranges and bookmarks. The user selects 0.25–100 MiB per file. The worker first builds the existing reviewed page-copy arrangement, then encodes candidate contiguous groups and measures the actual resulting bytes. Accepted files reuse those measured bytes; each physical output page appears exactly once and in order. It does not estimate file sizes from source bytes or silently divide a physical page.

If one physical page alone exceeds the maximum, the error identifies that output position and its actual encoded size. If the whole output already fits, the user is told to choose a smaller maximum for separate files. Shared resources may be repeated between parts; the combined output retains the existing 100 MiB budget. Group selection seeks fitting contiguous groups, without claiming maximal packing when PDF serialization sizes are not monotonic.

The worker limits encoding to 2,000 candidates and 1 GiB cumulative serialized bytes, inside the existing two-minute cancellable worker lifetime. Actual retained outputs are reopened for page count/geometry in the writer and use the existing independent split-preview pipeline and review checkbox before exclusive folder saving. Cancellation terminates the browser worker; original source bytes are untouched.

# PDF tag-tree remediation progress

This implements concrete, bounded existing-tag remediation and reviewed initial tagging of supported untagged page content toward A11/F30. It does **not** complete full tagging or establish PDF/UA or Section 508 conformance.

## Implemented

- Contained `tags-inspect` inventory of `StructTreeRoot`, every supported `K` child, `RoleMap`, and the complete bounded `ParentTree`. Reports include indirect structure IDs, parent/depth, inherited physical page, raw/resolved role, Alt/ActualText/Lang, existing element IDs, table attributes, MCIDs, MCR stream references and OBJR object references.
- Bounded traversal with cycle, shared-child, unresolved-reference, duplicate MCID ownership, structure parent, role-map cycle, number-tree ordering/limits and bidirectional ParentTree ownership checks. Unknown `K` forms cause a concrete refusal; unknown dictionary fields and objects are retained.
- Real native PDF mutations of existing tag roles, alternative text, language and eligible leaf ActualText; exact sibling `K` permutations change reading order without reassigning any content owner. Heading and existing list roles are supported; edited list/table structures must satisfy the implemented structural checks.
- Table TH/TD `Scope`, `RowSpan`, `ColSpan` and `Headers` updates when attributes are absent or a single Table dictionary, with no class attributes. Header associations require existing uniquely identified TH elements in the same Table and matching entries in a checked IDTree. Original byte-string IDs are reused. No IDs or IDTree entries are invented.
- Source SHA-256, inventory SHA-256, selection SHA-256 and output SHA-256 binding. Selected-field masking proves that other fields in edited tag dictionaries did not change. Every other source object is fingerprinted. The serialized copy is reopened and every indirect object/stream must match its intended fingerprint. The original page content and resource objects remain unchanged. Stream Length normalization can occur without changing stream payloads.
- Full bounded hierarchy navigation, selected-tag details, physical-page previews, MCID/MCR/OBJR relationship navigation, RoleMap/ParentTree inspection, staged changes, undo/redo, explicit exact-change review, cancellation/discard and save-as-copy. Rewritten pages use the independent PDF.js renderer. Tree verification is performed by the native re-open checks; the UI does not claim an independent standards validator.
- Initial untagged-content inventory uses a bounded PDF object/operator lexer, not string matching. It identifies complete BT–ET text objects, individual Image XObject Do operations and complete painted paths. Every candidate is source-bound by page, exact decoded-program byte range and SHA-256. Parenthesized/hex strings and text arrays remain operands, so operator-looking bytes in text cannot become candidate boundaries.
- Initial authoring starts with every group **unclassified**. Users select supported text/heading roles, Figures with required descriptions, Spans with verified replacement text, or explicit Artifact types. Whole-document reading order can be changed without changing drawing order. Document language and an explicit review of all classifications/order are required. Bulk current-page paragraph classification and Layout artifact marking are user-invoked actions with undo/redo. A visual marker gives an approximate text starting point or image center where available; it does not claim exact content bounds.
- Initial output contains a real indirect StructTreeRoot and Document element, indirect semantic elements, page MCIDs, StructParents, ParentTree entries, ParentTreeNextKey and MarkInfo/Marked. Artifacts are actual `/Artifact << /Type ... >> BDC ... EMC` sequences, excluded from the structure tree. The writer adds paired BDC/EMC wrappers around exact original decoded operator ranges, preserving drawing instructions/order and original resource/stream objects. Reopened replacement streams must match exactly; removing only the recorded inserted wrappers must recover each original decoded program hash.

## API contract

`desktop/pdf-tags-codec.cjs` exports `inspect(bytes)`, `write(bytes, selection)` and `MAX_BYTES`. The engine operations are `tags-inspect` and `tags-build`, with build options `{ selection }`.

`PdfTagsService` uses the established `ContainedServiceContext` and provides `inspect(sourceId, source)`, `build(sourceId, source, token, selection)`, `output(sourceId, source, token)`, `cancel`, `discard`, `dispose` and inherited `status`. A source is the existing source registry record with PDF bytes and fingerprint. Output retrieval requires the same source ID, source hash and operation token and checks the retained output hash.

The selection is:

```js
{
  inventorySha256,
  edits: [{ nodeId, changes: { role, alt, actualText, lang, scope, headers, rowSpan, colSpan } }],
  orders: [{ nodeId: '$root' /* or an existing structure ref */, children: ['stable K child ID'] }]
}
```

Only changed keys appear in `changes`; text/Scope/spans may be null to remove the entry. `headers` is an array of existing TH structure references; empty removes Headers. Node IDs use the original PDF indirect reference, e.g. `12 0 R`. Child IDs are stable relationship identities; all children must appear exactly once in an order selection. Edits are strictly allowlisted; unsupported mutation types are rejected.

For supported untagged inputs, inspection additionally returns `creation: { available, reason, candidates }`. Initial authoring uses the same operation/service/bridge and this mutually exclusive selection:

```js
{
  inventorySha256,
  edits: [], orders: [],
  create: {
    language: 'en-US', reviewed: true,
    items: [{
      candidateId: 'content-1-1', // Every source candidate exactly once, in reviewed reading order
      role: 'P',               // Text/heading, Figure, Span, or explicit Artifact
      alt: null, actualText: null, artifactType: null
    }]
  }
}
```

Figures require nonempty Alt; graphics representing text may use Span with explicit nonempty ActualText. Initial ActualText is limited to Span. Artifacts require Pagination, Layout, Page or Background and cannot carry Alt/ActualText. The receipt adds `createdTags` and `artifacts`; both are zero for existing-tree edits. No new IPC or engine operation names were added.

`src/pdf-tags-workspace.js` exports `PdfTagsWorkspace(reader, ui)` with `open()`, `close()` and `prepareDeparture()`. Bridge methods are `inspectPdfTags(id)`, `buildPdfTags(id, token, selection)`, `savePdfTags(id, token)`, `cancelPdfTags(id, token)`, and `discardPdfTags(id, token)`. The bridge's save-as-copy policy remains authoritative.

## Explicit limitations and remaining acceptance

- Initial authoring supports only fully inventoried untagged page programs in the bounded subset. Unsupported content refuses the entire initial plan with a concrete reason; there is no silently skipped page/group. No automatic semantic classification/reading order, OCR generation, text-object splitting/merging, initial list/table/link/form hierarchy construction or cross-parent moves. Initial semantic leaves are children of Document and require manual meaning/order acceptance.
- Artifact creation is supported for explicitly classified initial content groups. Editing/removing existing artifact sequences or converting existing tags into artifacts remains unsupported. `NonStruct` is never presented as an artifact substitute. Existing marked-content operators cause initial tagging to refuse rather than nesting new semantics over them.
- PDF 2.0/unknown document versions, namespace-aware structures, direct StructTreeRoot editing, unresolved custom roles, malformed structures, unsupported content children, signed/certified/permission-constrained/encrypted documents and XFA are refused or read-only as stated in the report. The writer emits PDF 1.7. PDF/UA identification metadata is preserved and is never added or upgraded.
- No class/revision-array/multiple-owner attribute editing or inferred table headers. Attributed role changes are refused where their semantic compatibility cannot be proved. Existing unsupported attributes remain intact. Table geometry, header correctness and content meaning require manual review.
- ActualText is deliberately limited to supported leaf text/formula roles containing existing MCID references; Figure, grouping, empty and OBJR-bearing tags require a specialist workflow. ActualText is replacement content, not a substitute for an image description.
- Existing-tree ParentTree checks establish structure ownership only; that path does not decode original streams to prove that each claimed MCID exists, has balanced marked-content operators, covers all meaningful content, or follows visual reading order. The initial-tag path checks the supported source grammar and inserts/validates every new wrapper, but semantic coverage still requires human acceptance of the chosen groups. Neither path audits font Unicode mapping, invisible/duplicate OCR content, language correctness or assistive-technology behavior.
- Initial content refusals include annotations/forms, optional-content layers, existing marked-content or structural ownership/orphan tags, nested Form XObjects, inline images, shading/pattern painting, external streams, DecodeParms, unknown/compatibility operators, unbalanced text/graphics/path syntax, image painting within text/path construction, graphics nesting/transforms within text, and text clipping. Source text labels are only decoded for the supported explicit built-in WinAnsi subset; other fonts receive a visual-review label. Approximate location markers are not text selection or reliable bounding boxes.
- The preservation checks cover parsed indirect objects and their dictionary fields/stream payloads. This is a fresh serialization, not an incremental byte-preserving update: cross-reference and object-stream containers, file offsets, original trailer syntax and revision history are not retained in the output. The original file must remain available. Nonstandard trailer extensions are outside this workflow's verification scope.
- Fixed input/output limit 100 MiB; 500 pages; 100,000 indirect objects; 300,000 graph visits / 80 graph levels; 2,000 tags / 48 hierarchy levels; 20,000 K relationships; 20,000 ParentTree/IDTree entries; 100,000 ParentTree slots; 4,096 characters per supported text field. Oversized structures are refused rather than truncated.
- Initial authoring additionally limits decoded content to 8 MiB/page and 32 MiB/document, 1,000 content groups, 200,000 tokens/page, 16 operand/string nesting levels and 64 graphics-state levels. The existing contained request/output limits also apply.
- Structural preservation verification is not accessibility certification. Full A11/F30 acceptance still requires broader content/group authoring, existing artifact conversion, list/table/link/form creation, recovery, standards validation and manual assistive-technology acceptance on representative PDFs.

## Concrete supported slice

The drawing comments panel now includes **Review XFDF import**, even when the PDF has no existing comments. The user chooses an explicit native XFDF file, inspects source-bound supported/omitted records, selects up to 200 records per copy, and prepares a new PDF copy. Nothing is selected automatically. Supported standard annotation types are Text, Line, Square, Circle, Polygon, PolyLine, Ink, Highlight, Underline, Squiggly and StrikeOut. Exact plain Unicode comments, author/subject text, supported literal date/state claims, physical page and geometry, standard RGB colors, opacity, border width/dashes and the first nine standard annotation flags are mapped. Text uses a disclosed generic vector comment icon. Lines support None/OpenArrow/ClosedArrow endings. Text markup currently requires axis-aligned rectangular quads.

Selected unique same-page imported parents receive standard IRT/RT reply links to their newly created PDF annotation references. A missing, duplicate, unsupported, self-linked, other-page, cyclic or overly deep parent is disclosed and omitted. A supported parent that is absent from the final selection leaves its child standalone and drops linked state history with an explicit result note. Existing PDF names are never treated as import targets; every new annotation receives a unique PDFix name, while its imported name is retained in the receipt.

The workspace reopens the actual output using PDF.js, checks page count and changed-page geometry, retains the original annotation identities/text/author/bounds, and independently locates each exact imported annotation by its new object reference and plain comment. It renders both original and prepared pages as real PDF artwork, including normal annotation appearances. Saving requires all changed pages, all input record pages and all result pages to have been shown, plus the user's review checkbox. Native save consumes the sealed reviewed output token; renderer bytes are not saved directly. A complete source/import/preservation receipt is available as literal JSON text.

## Parsing and preservation boundaries

Input must be exact valid UTF-8, XML 1.0, standard XFDF namespace, and at most 8 MiB. Parsing rejects DTD/entity declarations, non-declaration processing instructions, external file/appearance references, actions, scripts, embedded attachments and change-set elements. Foreign namespaced attributes cannot override standard fields. Rich/private/popup data is never executed and is individually disclosed as omitted. Only literal text is placed into UI elements; XML is not injected into HTML.

The contained engine receives canonical base64 bytes, never renderer paths or URLs. Fixed inspect/build operations have separate request bounds. Parent validators require exact inert receipt shapes, bounded literal fields/styles/geometry, finite coordinates, physical page identity, acyclic same-page parent references, exact source/XML/proposal/selection/output hashes and output inventory. Limits include 500 PDF pages, 1,000 import records, 200 selected records, 200,000 geometry numbers, 100,000 XML nodes, depth 16, 200 ink strokes per record, 10,000 resulting source annotations and 100 MiB PDF output.

The writer re-inspects the exact selected XML/source proposal before construction. It preserves every original indirect object and encoded content stream, appends new annotation dictionaries and font-free standard vector normal appearance streams, and changes only selected page Annots pointers. It copies the selected page annotation arrays rather than mutating shared arrays. Original annotation order/entries are retained. Only raw stream Length fields normalize to their unchanged encoded payload sizes as required by the writer.

The serialized copy is reopened natively. Full object fingerprints, retained object count, page geometry, trailer references, original annotation entries/order, new page references, exact Unicode comments, unique names and appearance stream hashes are checked against the constructed output. Receipts bind both source PDF and selected XFDF bytes. Cancel and final close clear the native selection/output lifecycle; final departure awaits cancellation and owned preview-document cleanup. The shared source PDF reader is never destroyed.

## Deliberate limits and remaining gates

This slice creates new comments; it does not merge changes into existing comments by NM, delete comments, import form values, create attachments or reproduce private Bluebeam/Revu properties, custom tools, custom appearances, rich text or grouping semantics. Imported file IDs, dates, names, authors and states are source claims, not authentication. Repeating an import creates another set of new annotations.

Coordinates must fit the target physical page's visible media/crop intersection. Unsupported source-page transforms, non-unit UserUnit, non-right-angle rotation, encrypted/signed/certified/XFA or unsafe structural graphs are refused by the preserving engine. Flags that hide an annotation are retained and disclosed; those comments may be visible only in result text. Stroke portions extending outside their source annotation rectangle are clipped by the normal appearance bounding box. Text-markup quad corners are preserved literally; no reading-order reconstruction is promised.

This is a coherent saved code slice with source syntax/bundle verification only. No runtime app, browser, native worker, XML corpus or Revu/Acrobat acceptance tests were run, in accordance with the current user instruction. # Print marks implementation · 2026-10-12

F64 adds crop, bleed-boundary and registration marks to an explicitly selected set of physical pages. The engine entry point is `buildPrintMarks(bytes, draft)` from `desktop/pdf-print-marks-codec.cjs`, dispatched inside the fixed contained engine as `print-marks-build`. The desktop service is `PdfPrintMarksService`; its `build(sourceId, source, token, draft)` accepts the opened PDF source object and returns `{token, bytes, report}`. `output`, `cancel`, `discard`, `status` and `dispose` follow the contained decoration-service pattern. Renderer calls are `buildPdfPrintMarks(id, token, draft)`, `savePdfPrintMarks(id, token)`, `cancelPdfPrintMarks(id, token)` and `discardPdfPrintMarks(id, token)`.

The version 1 draft names zero-based selected pages, millimeter or point units, four bleed distances, mark offset, line width, one RGB ink color, three mark-type switches, and acknowledgment that MediaBox/CropBox may expand. The writer uses the selected page's leaf TrimBox where present and otherwise uses the visible MediaBox/CropBox intersection as its effective trim. When that selected page has no leaf TrimBox, the writer materializes one at the effective trim coordinates; the receipt reports `trimMaterialized: true` and independent reopening verifies the exact geometry. Existing leaf TrimBox values are retained. MediaBox/CropBox may be inherited. UserUnit is checked at the leaf on selected pages; non-default selected units are refused, while unselected pages retain their page dictionaries and units untouched. It keeps existing page content references and stream bytes and writes new vector strokes outside the effective trim area. It expands MediaBox and CropBox enough to include the marks.

The preview renders each selected page from the original and independently reopened output and reports exact TrimBox, MediaBox and CropBox coordinates, including whether it materialized an effective TrimBox. Every selected page must be reviewed before save. Build refuses signed, certified, encrypted, XFA, malformed, unsupported content-stream, unsupported box and selected non-default UserUnit inputs. The output is a new copy bound to the source fingerprint and output hash; no source overwrite is offered by this service.

The bleed settings reserve space and draw boundary marks. They do not generate or extend artwork into a bleed area. The selected ink is a single visible RGB color, not process-color separations; this work makes no claim about color management, PDF/X, PDF/A or other print compliance. Page rotations are preserved and marks use the PDF page coordinate system; unusual source graphics state can affect rendering, so compare each actual source/output page before saving. Existing TrimBox geometry is not altered.

# Free local Windows read aloud — F44 / R43 / R46

Implemented a Windows x64 plain-text speech adapter using the installed .NET Framework `System.Speech` / SAPI speech engines. It supports installed voice and language enumeration, rate selection, asynchronous play, native pause/resume, stop, per-word character progress and completion. No paid speech service, cloud API, account connection, voice download or speech audio file export is implemented. Voice availability and behavior depend on installed Windows-compatible SAPI engines and the default Windows audio device; this does not expose every Windows OneCore/natural voice.

## Renderer and source integration contract

`ReadAloudWorkspace(root, {sourceProvider, highlight, announce, api})` prepares a readonly text preview before explicit Play. The scope control offers selected text, current page and whole document. Unsupported or missing text/voices produce visible errors. A partial source extraction is disclosed separately from batching. A provider `nextCursor` enables Continue reading, which prepares the next batch for review and explicit playback. It never silently restarts the first page or calls a speech service from document content.

The provider receives `{scope, cursor, maxChunks:128, maxChars:200000, maxChunkChars:4096, signal}` and returns `{chunks:[{text,page?,start?,sourceLabel?}], nextCursor?, partial?, notice?}`. Chunk text and source offsets use UTF-16 character indices. Providers must keep document/revision identity bound to the cursor, use bounded/lazy extraction, and check cancellation before and after extraction. `page` is one-based; `start` is the chunk's first source character. Native progress is translated to `{chunkIndex,page?,start:chunk.start+wordOffset,length,sourceLabel?}`. Highlight is cleared with `{clear:true}` on terminal state, stop and departure. Physical page scope in a rich document editor depends on its actual page model; a paragraph/block substitute must be disclosed by that provider.

The API methods are `speechVoices()`, `speechStart({chunks,voice,rate})`, `speechControl({sessionId,command})`, `speechRelease()` and `onSpeechEvent(callback) -> unsubscribe`. `speechStart` resolves after native startup with `{sessionId}`. Commands are only `pause`, `resume` and `stop`. Public events bind `{sessionId,type}`; progress adds `{chunkIndex,start,length}`, chunk events add `{chunkIndex}` and errors add `{message}`. The IPC owner must come from the approved application sender, never from renderer options. Main-process wiring/build integration and PDF/document source providers are owned by their integration files.

## Native boundary and ownership

`LocalSpeechService` accepts bounded plain text and source metadata only, never document paths, PDF bytes, arbitrary operations, SSML, output paths or executable arguments from the renderer. Voice IDs must come from that owner's successful installed-voice enumeration. Each batch has at most 128 chunks, 4096 characters per chunk and 200,000 characters total. The service spawns the fixed helper with shell disabled, a minimal Windows environment, a random private token and a random session ID. All native commands and events must bind that token/session. Native event schemas, chunk order, monotonic word offsets and output bounds are checked before renderer callbacks.

The helper is pinned to a deliberately reviewed source SHA-256 constant and the executable hash in its generated manifest. Linked helper paths are rejected. A per-user native mutex prevents two PDFix helper processes from owning speech simultaneously. The helper operates outside the document AppContainer because it needs Windows voice and audio-device access. Installed speech engines are trusted Windows/vendor components; PDFix implements no network retrieval or cloud speech path.

A self-assigned Windows job permits one process, caps process memory at 256 MiB and CPU time at 120 seconds, and uses kill-on-job-close. Independent checks terminate on parent death/PID reuse, a 15-second missing heartbeat or two-hour lifetime. The parent limits startup to 30 seconds. Each native line is capped at 131,072 output bytes and cumulative output at 24 MiB/100,000 events; input lines are bounded, command queues are capped and only fixed commands are accepted. Prompt/chunk changes and progress emission are serialized so late progress cannot point into a following chunk. Final state is published to the renderer only after observed process exit. If termination is not observed within the kill deadline, the service retains exclusive ownership and disables further speech until app restart.

Stopping during text extraction aborts the provider and invalidates its generation. Stopping during native startup releases the owner even before a session ID returns. Leaving the workspace aborts extraction, releases native speech, waits for pending work and removes the event listener. Text is retained in renderer memory for review/playback; parent chunk references are released at native termination. No persistent speech-text or audio output file is created.

# Reading capacity estimate

PDFix can report host memory availability, logical CPU capacity, a bounded CPU model string, and graphics feature status supplied by the app. The estimate reserves 768 MiB and budgets three times a PDF's file size in memory, capped at 1 GiB. It also reports the current whole-file tool, page, range-assembly, and concurrent-read limits.

The Settings panel offers a manual refresh and labels the PDF size as an estimate. PDF complexity, graphics content, other applications, and current workload affect responsiveness; this report does not promise a lag-free size. Graphics information is limited to status fields supplied by the app and does not query drivers or run benchmarks.

The native report is available through the existing authorized IPC/preload bridge. PDF opening attaches a validated reading profile; native large-file admission uses the same memory formula as the report. PCs with less than 2 GiB currently available memory, fewer than four logical cores, or reported disabled/software graphics receive an 8-million-pixel page preview ceiling instead of 16 million. Multipage preview totals adapt to twice that ceiling, up to the existing 32-million-pixel maximum. Original document bytes and the existing image decoding limit are unchanged. Source-read concurrency is bounded to one through four calls from the profile. This profile is selected when opening; refreshing Settings updates the estimate, not an already opened document's profile.

No document scan, benchmark, hardware driver query, external request, or performance test was run. Reading remains limited to 1 GiB and 500 pages, with available-memory admission. Whole-file editing/export tools remain limited to 100 MiB; source assembly still rejects an individual range over 64 MiB or a whole-source request.

# Contained structural redaction verification

Saved 2026-10-04. Native original-source parsing and candidate clean-image verification now use only the packaged fixed AppContainer engine. The unrestricted Node worker adapter and worker source have been removed. The renderer retains its existing bounded clean-image rendering/writer and reviewed preview; this migration covers the native independent structural/save gate, not a new rendering engine.

## Integration

`RedactionService` keeps `verify(id,source,token,candidateBytes,draft)`, `output(id,currentSource,token)`, token-only `cancel(token)` and `discard(token)`. **Source is now the owned `store.source(id)` object**, including `ext`, bytes and fingerprint. Output returns a detached Buffer as before; the independently sealed report remains `service.verified.result`. Main must pass current source to output and use that report SHA for the existing exclusive, source-bound copy save. Verification returns the existing pageCount/layout/regions/cleanupOnly/sha256 fields plus version, verified, source/output byte counts and source/inspection/draft hashes.

Cancel/discard are asynchronous. `dispose()` awaits observed termination and cleanup; `status()` uses the shared package status cache and live transaction/engine state. Await disposal before replacing the service after renderer loss, retain the failed closed service on unsafe cleanup rejection, and catch disposal failure during quit. Root owns main/preload/status/lifecycle changes.

## Fixed phases and receipts

`redaction-inspect` receives only the original PDF and empty options. The child refuses encrypted, permission-controlled, signed, XFA, malformed/excessive structures and invalid page/image geometry using the existing redaction source rules. Its compact inert inspection contains the exact original SHA and byte length, 1–100 page geometry records and form-presence flag.

`redaction-verify` receives only the candidate clean-image PDF and `{inspection,draft}`. The adapter exclusively supplies the validated first-phase geometry and immutable draft. Pure parent/child validators independently check exact object keys, geometry math, mark bounds, 144/180/216 DPI, 500 marks, 8,192-pixel edges, 16 million pixels/page and 100 million pixels/job. Original SHA, canonical inspection SHA, draft SHA and candidate SHA are bound to the returned receipt. A token-bound transaction spans both child jobs, so cancellation between phases cannot resume verification or release a saved copy.

The contained child reopens the candidate using the existing strict clean-image verifier: flat exact page tree and allowed object keys, image-only RGB/Flate streams with exact expected dimensions, black pixels throughout expanded masks, canonical image/content stream bytes, no metadata/protection/unreferenced objects and exact canonical whole-file serialization. This canonical reserialization is a proof step in the contained child. Rendering cannot preserve selectable original text; the output intentionally remains the existing clean-image redacted copy. The source fingerprint and original SHA, output SHA and sealed receipt SHA are rechecked when main requests saving.

Both phases keep the ordinary **2 MiB request**, **100 MiB input/candidate** and **32 MiB outer result** limits; redaction receipts are further bounded to 64 KiB. No raw RGB/base64 images or extra file slots are introduced. Existing decoder guards, shared two-job lease, one-job family slot, pinned-byte launch verification, AppContainer capabilities, Job Object limits, observed broker close, cleanup-before-release and permanent unsafe failure closure are unchanged. There is no unrestricted fallback.

# Reliability, performance, and workspace release gates

These are the user's top release priorities for PDFix. They govern the existing full product scope and free-app requirement; they do not remove previously adopted capabilities or establish a release date. “Never corrupt” and “100% bug-free” are product goals, not guarantees that software can prove. Release decisions require executed evidence on real files and supported hardware. Source compilation alone establishes neither output integrity nor runtime performance.

## Acceptance matrix — planned, not yet passed

| Priority | Release acceptance to measure | Failure rule and evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original and output preservation | For every save, sign, split, redact, page rewrite, and drawing measurement export route, hash the original before/after; create a separate output; verify saved disk bytes match reviewed bytes; independently reopen every resulting file. Exercise valid, malformed, encrypted, signed, interrupted, cancelled, out-of-space, and permission-denied inputs within each route's supported boundary. | A mismatch, unreadable output, unsupported structure, partial save, or unverified result is a failed operation. Keep the original unchanged, clean temporary output, and give a specific error. Do not report success from a writer callback alone. Record input/output hashes, independent reader results, and failure-path observations. |
| Signing and redaction correctness | For visual signatures, verify appearance and placement after independent reopen; for certificate signatures, verify cryptographic status, trust result, byte range, and any post-sign change under the supported policy. For redaction, inspect text extraction, page pixels, objects/streams, metadata, annotations, attachments, and saved bytes; verify every affected page and disclose flattening or other losses. | Fail closed if the chosen signing or redaction mode cannot prove its stated result. Do not call a visual signature a certificate signature. Do not call cropping or a black overlay redaction. Record independent validation and negative controls. |
| Blueprint precision | On representative engineering sheets, compare geometry, scale, calibration, rotated/cropped coordinates, markups, measurements, takeoff totals, and exported/reopened results against known reference values. Define per-tool tolerances in physical units and pixels before acceptance; test edge cases and calibration changes. | Refuse or clearly disable measurements when page scale/units are unknown or inconsistent. No invented precision. Log reference values, observed error, calibration state, and output round trips. |
| Large-document responsiveness | On a documented realistic Windows hardware tier, use real 500-page PDFs and 300 MB PDF/drawing sets. Record cold open, first useful page, page jump, scroll, zoom, search, thumbnail navigation, memory peak, cancellation, and sustained interaction over repeated sessions. Set numeric p50/p95 targets from baseline measurements before release and compare regressions against them. | No unbounded render/text/thumbnail work for the entire set on opening. Keep only a bounded visible-page window and nearby prefetch in active memory, cancel stale work, and recover from resource pressure without losing edits. Record hardware, corpus, timing traces, peak memory, and crash/hang results. |
| Workspace clarity | Drawing, Document, and Pages have separate primary workspaces with task-specific tools and clear return paths. Observe first-time and keyboard/screen-reader users completing representative drawing review, document editing, and page organization tasks. Measure task completion, wrong-workspace starts, backtracking, and time to the intended tool; set targets after baseline observation. | Fix unclear routing, hidden controls, focus traps, and repeated cross-workspace detours before release. Use contextual tools and short explanations; avoid banners or controls that crowd the document. Record task scripts and observation results. |

## Execution order and pending beta gates

1. Inventory every writer/output path and its failure modes. Apply fail-closed new-copy saving, original preservation, independent reopening, and mode-specific validation to each route. Include interrupted/cancelled operations and incomplete disk writes.
2. Build a real-file corpus for documents, difficult PDFs, drawing sheets, signatures, and redactions. Define expected visual/structural outcomes and engineering tolerances before running acceptance.
3. Measure the 500-page/300 MB scenarios on a named realistic hardware tier. Use traces to choose numeric interaction and memory budgets; then implement and verify bounded visible-page virtualization, cancellation, and regression limits.
4. Evaluate Drawing, Document, and Pages with representative users and assistive technology. Keep the main actions task-specific and discoverable while preserving all planned features in appropriate workspaces.
5. Release beta only after the applicable integrity, security, corpus, performance, accessibility, installation, and usability gates have executed and passed. Record known limitations against the supported format matrix. A source build, a single fixture, or a successful preview cannot close these gates.

The current coding pass does not execute runtime, UI, PDF, hardware, or corpus tests. Every acceptance row above remains pending until those checks are performed and recorded.

# PDFix sandbox, explained

For a drawing reviewer: PDFix processes a PDF in a separate, restricted Windows process. Think of it as a locked workroom. The large-file reader gives it a private copy of the drawing to read and one private page file to write. It requests no network capabilities, prevents child processes and limits memory and time. The viewer receives a prepared page instead of loading the entire drawing into RAM. These are coded controls; complete runtime isolation and drawing-fidelity acceptance remain pending.

The sandbox is not a setting your dad needs to enlarge or configure. It is part of PDFix. A startup failure means PDFix cannot start the restricted process, so it stops rather than running an unrestricted parser. It is distinct from the separate Windows Sandbox desktop application.

Windows code 203 (`ERROR_ENVVAR_NOT_FOUND`) means a required environment setting was not found. The reported stage was `launch`, before PDF parsing began. This is not evidence of an oversized PDF or an antivirus block. Which missing setting Windows attempted to resolve is not identified by that code.

The repair supplies this small, explicit Windows-location allowlist to the trusted broker without inheriting PATH, keys or unrelated environment settings. It does not grant the parser additional filesystem access.

The restricted child receives an explicitly sorted, double-null-terminated Unicode environment block. Child profile/temp settings point to its private staging folder, and Windows installation/drive settings are supplied explicitly. All containment checks and resource limits remain.

The paged error message now distinguishes code 203 from possible loader/security blocks. Actual opening of the user's drawing is required to determine whether these environment changes resolve the failure. No PDF/native/UI/performance tests were run during this coding pass.

The user reported the exact Windows status `0xc0000142` after the prior environment and DLL-search changes. This is DLL initialization failure. It is not proof of a missing DLL or a damaged PDF, and the status alone does not identify the failing module.

- Paged processing creates a uniquely named, hidden desktop with an explicit private DACL and low integrity label.
