## Implemented route

- A user opens Scan to PDF, enumerates Windows WIA scanners, explicitly selects one device, chooses flatbed or simplex feeder, 150/300/600 dpi and color/grayscale/black-and-white, then presses Scan. No native acquisition begins during startup or document opening.
- `desktop/native/ScannerCapture.cs` connects only the selected enumerated WIA scanner. It selects the WIA flatbed/feeder category; legacy WIA one-child trees use root document-handling source selection. WIA 2 feeders use `FRONT_ONLY` and `PAGES=1`; direct `Item.Transfer` repeats until the requested page limit or `WIA_ERROR_PAPER_EMPTY`. A flatbed page uses `CommonDialog.ShowTransfer`, allowing native progress/cancellation after the explicit Scan click. Repeated flatbed captures are retained as one pending renderer collection.
- The helper requests the universally supported WIA BMP transfer format, checks single-frame dimensions and collection pixel budgets, then normalizes with the Windows WIA `ImageProcess` Convert filter to PNG. The app checks actual PNG format, dimensions and frame count before accepting a page. This does not install or download a driver or launch a vendor program.
- `desktop/scanner-service.cjs` owns staging directories and a fixed executable path with a build-manifest SHA-256 pin. It passes only fixed operation names and validated device/settings arguments, using `spawn` with `shell:false`. It exposes opaque capture IDs and metadata, not arbitrary source/output paths or commands. Each captured PNG receives regular-file/path checks, signature/IHDR/chunk-framing/CRC/IEND checks, byte/pixel budgets, and a SHA-256 content fingerprint. Import rechecks fingerprints and PNG framing before returning bytes to the app-owned FileStore route.
- The native helper self-assigns a Windows Job object with a 768 MiB process memory limit, one-process limit and kill-on-close. Service enumeration has a 30-second deadline; capture has a 10-minute deadline. Cancellation terminates the owned helper, waits for observed process close, and completes output cleanup before settling the operation. Renderer destruction uses `disposeOwner`; service disposal and next initialization clean app-owned pending directories. Cleanup errors are reported, rather than represented as successful cleanup.
- Pending batches are limited to 10 pages total, 32 MiB and 16 million pixels (8192 pixels per side) per PNG, 100 MiB aggregate and 64 million pixels aggregate, matching the existing image collection. A page-limit result explicitly says more paper may remain. An empty feeder before the first image is an error. A cancellation, jam or failed capture discards the current batch's partial images while previously completed captures remain pending.
- The renderer can discard captures or import them to the existing image workspace. Parent integration saves scan PNG copies exclusively into a user-chosen durable folder and persists the collection so existing ordering, rotation, adjustments, reviewed PDF preview and exclusive Save PDF copy can operate. Original documents are untouched. Scanning does not add OCR/searchable text automatically.

## Integration contract

`createScannerService({root})` / `new ScannerService({root})`, where `root` is an absolute application-owned staging directory; call `await init()` before use. The default helper is `dist/native/scanner/PDFix.Scanner.exe`.

Methods:

- `listDevices(owner)` returns `{devices:[{id,name,manufacturer}],backend:'Windows WIA'}` and scopes the selected-device allowlist to that owner.
- `capture(owner,{deviceId,source,maxPages,dpi,color})` returns `{captureId,pages:[{id,name,ext:'png',byteLength,width,height,dpi}],completion}`. `source` is `flatbed` or `feeder`; flatbed requires `maxPages:1`, feeder accepts 1–10 within the remaining collection budget. Completion is `single-page`, `feeder-empty` or `page-limit`.
- `takeCapture(owner,captureId)` returns validated page records `{name,ext:'png',bytes,width,height,dpi}` for trusted FileStore staging. After staging and collection persistence succeed, call `releaseCapture(owner,captureId)`. Do not remove prior captures when FileStore staging fails.
- `releaseCapture(owner,captureId)`, `cancel(owner)`, `disposeOwner(owner)` and `dispose()` remove only owned, validated staging directories and files. No directory deletion follows a renderer-supplied path.

`ScannerWorkspace(root,{announce,beforeImport,onImported,setGuard})` exposes `open()`, `prepareDeparture()`, `releaseDeparture()` and `dispose({prepared})`. It expects narrow preload methods `scannerDevices()`, `scannerCapture(options)`, `scannerCancel()`, `scannerImport(captureIds)` and `scannerDiscard(captureIds)`. `beforeImport()` runs before native import to finish the current editor/drawing departure guard; returning false aborts import. Cancelled native directory/import selection retains captures and the caller restores its prepared editor state. `onImported(result)` runs after the scanner operation has finished, permitting navigation into the existing image workspace without waiting on its own active operation. A modal caller supplies `setGuard(value)` to compose pending scan/busy protection with the existing editor's guard; the standalone default calls `editorGuard(value)` directly. Import/discard IDs must be bounded, unique, owner-checked and serialized in the main-process integration. Handle import errors before releasing captures and restore application guards around navigation.

Build integration: call `buildScannerHelper()` from `scripts/build-scanner-helper.mjs` during Vite's native build stage. It uses the installed Framework64 C# compiler with `/platform:x64 /warnaserror+`, references Windows .NET libraries and outputs the executable, source/executable SHA-256 manifest and `NOTICE.txt` in `dist/native/scanner`. The Windows package builder must verify the scanner manifest/file hash and include it in its native inventory; its existing `dist` copy includes all scanner assets. Compilation does not launch the helper or touch a scanner.

## Trust and remaining limits

WIA acquisition and normalization execute in a full-user-access device helper outside the document AppContainer because driver/device access is needed. The helper's Job object limits its own process, not the out-of-process Windows WIA service or vendor driver. Windows/vendor image codecs run before PNG framing validation; a malicious or broken driver is outside document-parser containment. The app makes no HTTP requests or accepts network addresses/URLs in the scanner API; an explicitly selected installed WIA device may use its driver's own USB or network transport.

Image normalization/preview/PDF construction in the existing `ImageWorkspace` use browser WebWorkers in Electron's sandboxed, context-isolated renderer without Node integration. They are not the fixed native document AppContainer route. Main-process PNG checks validate framing and integrity, not compressed-pixel decoding or semantic artwork correctness. The image workspace independently previews/reopens the generated PDF and requires review before copy export; hardware quality, orientation, exact page region and silent driver truncation still require human inspection.

App cancellation observes helper exit and discards current outputs. It cannot promise that the physical feeder or Windows/vendor driver stops immediately; mechanical movement or a busy-device state can continue outside the helper. Native dialog handling, error recovery and driver teardown must be verified on real hardware. Driver-specific settings, automatic duplex, TWAIN-only devices, vendor-only protocols, arbitrary custom resolutions, hardware buttons and scanner fleet compatibility are not implemented. Current WIA automation source-tree/property support is an intentionally bounded compatibility route and may reject drivers that do not expose or honor the required settings. The scanner's default acquisition area is retained; cropping can be reviewed in the image workspace. A typical full A4/Letter page at 600 dpi exceeds the existing image-workspace 16-million-pixel limit and must be captured at lower dpi; the app rejects it transparently and does not silently downsize or change the requested resolution.

## Main/preload integration

# PDFix Security Sandbox

Status: native broker source compiled with the latest changes. OS behavior and adversarial isolation checks remain deferred. This is not a completed security certification.

## Native PDF jobs

Compression and password processing run the pinned qpdf runtime through the native Windows broker. Launch fails closed if the broker, manifest, hashes, staging checks, AppContainer setup, token validation or Job Object setup fails. There is no direct unrestricted qpdf fallback.

The broker creates a per-job AppContainer with no requested capabilities, then checks the suspended child token for the exact expected AppContainer SID and zero capability SIDs. It verifies membership in the configured Job Object before allowing execution. No network capability is granted. Only three explicit pipe handles are inherited.

The app-owned job directory receives the job SID's modify grant. The immutable input and ownership markers receive read grants; the staged, hash-checked runtime receives read/execute grants. Reparse points in staging paths and their ancestors are rejected. The runtime is copied into the job folder so package engine ACLs are not expanded for individual jobs.

The Job Object has a one-process limit, a 512 MiB process and job memory limit, a 120-second CPU budget and kill-on-close. Child-process creation is restricted. A monotonic 115-second wall-clock watchdog runs concurrently with stdin forwarding; blocked password/argument pipes cannot hold up that watchdog. Parent-process termination is also monitored. Broker stdin must arrive within five seconds, remain under 16 KiB and contain no NUL byte. Secrets travel over stdin and are cleared from the broker's byte buffer after the job.

Broker forwarding caps each diagnostic pipe at 2 MiB; each engine applies its own narrower output bound. The staging watchdog allows only the known PDF and ownership files, rejects new directory trees, and stops a job if an individual PDF exceeds 100 MiB. Temporary-file cleanup deletes only explicitly recognized files and profiles. Cleanup failures remain visible rather than silently reporting success.

## Limits that remain

The staging watchdog is not an OS disk quota: a process can allocate disk space between observations. AppContainer storage also needs a future quota/containment review. An ordinary AppContainer retains Windows access to resources deliberately exposed to application packages; this is not a claim that every system file and registry key is inaccessible. A less-privileged AppContainer policy has not been implemented.

Node worker threads for PDF verification, redaction and Office decoding are responsiveness and memory boundaries, not separate OS security sandboxes. The Electron renderer uses its own Chromium sandbox and restricted IPC boundary. The native qpdf broker does not make every document decoder OS-isolated.

Source compilation is not evidence that Windows ACL propagation, token values, executable loading, cancellation, parent death or malicious-input containment work on supported systems. Hidden runtime checks, clean-machine packaging checks and independent security review remain release gates.

# Local search across explicitly chosen files

Saved source implementation, 2026-10-04. Runtime testing is deferred by user request.

Search selected files is available from Files, Workspaces and the action finder. The native picker accepts up to ten PDF, DOCX, RTF or supported UTF-8 text/data files. It reads only chosen sources, canonicalizes duplicate paths, retains immutable snapshots and fingerprints, and reports unreadable or unsupported choices individually. Choosing search sources does not change the opened document or add items to recent history.

Users choose which picked files to search, enter a phrase and select case sensitivity or whole-word matching. Matching collapses whitespace while retaining source offsets and literal excerpts. Results include filename and physical PDF page or source/extracted-text line, with fifty results per screen. Each file has an extraction report, including partial failures and omitted content. Opening a result explicitly reopens its original using the searched SHA-256; changed originals are refused. PDF results jump to the selected physical page. Document line references refer to saved or extracted text, not Word pagination. Opening a document exposes its Find controls with the searched phrase; source-text editors additionally select the precise result only when their entire displayed text still equals the saved source, so a restored recovery draft is not mistaken for the searched copy.

PDF.js searches selectable text locally, with its own owned loading task. Password-protected PDFs are skipped, copying restrictions are respected, and scans are not OCRed automatically. DOCX searches extracted body text; headers, footers, drawings and other unsupported content are omitted. RTF uses the supported local text adapter. Plain data files require valid UTF-8 and reject NUL/binary content. No active document content is executed or external document resource fetched.

Bounds: ten chosen files; 100 MiB combined source bytes; PDF at most 100 MiB and 500 physical pages; DOCX/RTF at most 10 MiB each; text/data at most 2 MiB each; page/extracted text at most 2 MiB, PDF text at most 50,000 runs per page; 32 MiB aggregate extracted UTF-8 text; 2,000 displayed matches; query at most 200 characters; owned extraction waits at most thirty seconds (document worker forty-five), with a two-minute per-file deadline. Native snapshots expire after thirty minutes. Cancel fences pending results by generation and destroys only owned search tasks/workers; close discards the native snapshot and results; the parent clears owned snapshot buffers on discard, expiry or renderer loss. Choosing or opening a native source must finish before departure.

The PDF and DOCX extraction workers run in Chromium's existing sandboxed renderer context, not the native contained document engine. This feature does not expand native-engine containment claims.

Later runtime acceptance must cover actual-file native picking and cancellation, duplicates, mixed formats, scanned/password/restricted PDFs, Unicode/whitespace/whole-word matching, filenames and physical references, limits/partial reports, snapshot expiry, changing originals, dirty-editor departure, worker disposal, keyboard/screen-reader behavior and result opening. # Local spell-checking progress — F46 / R45 / R46

The source implementation uses the Windows Spell Checking API and already installed language providers. It needs no paid API, subscription, feature unlock, dictionary download or document upload. Windows x64 and an installed supported language dictionary are required. A missing helper or unsupported language produces an explicit explanation; there is no remote fallback.

## Implemented source

- `desktop/native/LocalSpelling.cs` exposes fixed JSON `languages` and `check` operations through the Windows COM spell-checker factory. It calls `ISpellChecker.Check` and `Suggest`, returns UTF-16 offsets and bounded suggestions, and has no API for changing or registering Windows dictionaries. Each request owns and releases its COM interfaces on the STA thread. No renderer-supplied file path is accepted.
- `desktop/local-spelling-service.cjs` validates the pinned helper manifest, source SHA-256, executable SHA-256, request-bound response, offsets, exact source words and suggestions. Text is limited to 100,000 UTF-16 units per call, native findings to 400 and suggestions to eight per finding. Native requests are at most 800,000 UTF-8 bytes and output at most 1 MiB.
- The native helper attaches itself to a one-process Windows job with a 256 MiB memory limit and ten seconds of process CPU time. It checks the actual spawning parent and keeps an open process handle to detect parent death. The service enforces a 15-second wall deadline, bounded pipes, cancellation and observed process exit. A helper whose termination is not observed within five seconds closes the service to further work.
- Personal words live in a main-process-selected PDFix storage file. Saves replace a language list atomically through a newly created temporary file, with symlink checks, serialized writes, a 2 MiB file limit, 10,000 words per language and 20,000 overall. The editor supports adding, editing and clearing words. Personal words and session ignored words are matched by NFC normalization and lowercasing, then filtered locally. Windows `Add`, `AutoCorrect`, dictionary registration and global dictionary edits are never called. Personal words are accepted during checking but are not injected into Windows suggestion lists.
- `src/spell-check-workspace.js` provides language selection, explicit local checking, source-bound findings, suggestion replacement, ignore once, ignore all, reset ignored words, personal dictionary controls, cancel and departure cleanup. It scans sources in bounded chunks, up to one million UTF-16 units and 1,000 displayed findings. Reaching a native or workspace limit is reported as incomplete review. Suggestions are rendered as text. Replacement callbacks recheck current revision, text and edit permission before invoking the source editor.
- `src/document-spelling.js` provides optional TipTap underline decorations and paragraph-to-ProseMirror source mappings. Code blocks, inline code and embedded atoms are blanked in check text. Decorations clear on any document edit, so previous results cannot label newly edited words. Identifiers, source/code, formulas, paths and receipt inputs remain opted out by default; a prose-control helper makes the choice explicit.
- Read-only PDF review uses page-number segments and a locate callback. The generic workspace disables replacements for a read-only snapshot and never changes PDF text, permissions, font compatibility or source bytes. Supported PDF editing must still pass the application's existing edit checks.
- `src/document-text-tools.js` connects Spell check and Read aloud toolbar buttons to modal panels. Opening preserves the captured selection and fences it by file identity and editor revision. ## Integration contract

Construct `LocalSpellingService` in the trusted main process with `{helperPath, dictionaryPath}`; neither path comes from a renderer request. The default helper path is `dist/native/local-spelling/PDFix.LocalSpelling.exe`. `dictionaryPath` must be an absolute app-owned file under user data. Expose only the following renderer calls through the existing validated owner-window IPC boundary:

| Renderer method | Main service method | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `localSpellingLanguages()` | `languages({signal})` | `{languages:[{tag,label}],provider,notice}` |
| `localSpellingCheck(request)` | `check(request,{signal})` | Request `{text,language,revision,ignoreWords?}`; response `{revision,language,findings,truncated,provider}` |
| `localSpellingDictionary()` | `dictionary()` | `{version:1,languages:{[tag]:words}}` |
| `localSpellingUpdateDictionary(request)` | `updateDictionary(request)` | `{language,words}` replaces that language's complete list; empty list clears it |
| `localSpellingCancel()` | `cancel()` | Waits for observed exit, returns whether cleanup completed |

Dispose the service when its owner closes. A finding is `{start,length,word,action,suggestions}` with action `suggest`, `replace` or `delete`. Empty replacement text represents deletion. A revision is an integer or nonempty bounded source-identity string; the service echoes it and the source UI checks it again before editing.

Construct `SpellCheckWorkspace(root,{getSnapshot,applyReplacement,onLocate,onFindings,announce,api})`. `getSnapshot` returns `{text,revision,sourceLabel,segments?,readOnly?,reason?,optOut?}`. PDF segments are `{start,end,pageNumber}`; editable-document segments also include `from`. `applyReplacement({revision,start,length,word,replacement})` must use the editor's ordinary Undo/recovery transaction and return false if it refuses the edit. `onLocate(finding,snapshot)` receives a page number where available. `onFindings(findings,snapshot)` connects editor underlines. The panel exports `open`, `check`, `sourceChanged`, `prepareDeparture` and `dispose`.

Rich editors can register `DocumentSpellingHighlights`, produce text using `documentSpellingSnapshot(editor,revision,label)`, map a finding using `documentSpellingRange(snapshot,finding)`, and render findings through `setDocumentSpellingHighlights(editor,findings,snapshot)`. The source adapter must fence edits against stale revisions and use its existing recovery size limits. Source/code text can use an explicit opt-in; native input checking must still be bounded.

Existing entries must agree with the source element IDs. Extended, malformed, cyclic, duplicate, unordered or overlapping IDTree structures are explicitly refused. Changing an ID does not silently retarget existing Headers: any old references must be explicitly corrected in the same draft, or the build fails.

Touched tables require direct TR children or supported THead / TBody / TFoot groups, a maximum of one caption and one group of each kind, and TH / TD row children. The bounded grid accounts for spans and refuses overlapping cells, spans beyond the final row, holes/irregular widths and oversized grids. Header arrays must point uniquely to other TH cells in the same containing Table and match the IDTree; recursive header cycles are refused. Reordering table children checks the final grid/order. These checks establish structural consistency; they do not infer which header has the correct meaning or certify table accessibility.

ListNumbering can be edited on L tags with absent attributes or a single List owner. The supported PDF 1.7 values are None, Disc, Circle, Square, Decimal, UpperRoman, LowerRoman, UpperAlpha and LowerAlpha. Existing visible labels are preserved. Printable, noninteractive leaf Form tags can receive PrintField Role (rb / cb / pb / tv), lowercase checked (on / off / neutral) and Desc properties. A checked state requires rb or cb. Interactive/object references, nested Form structures, class attributes, revisioned attributes and multiple attribute owners are refused. Existing Link tags continue to support Alt and Lang corrections while their object references, destinations and actions remain unchanged. Source scripts/actions are never executed by tag authoring or page previews; PDF.js previews disable evaluation and XFA.

The trusted selection/result validators accept only the declared mutations and verify readback values, table membership and header identities. Receipts retain source, inventory, selection and output SHA bindings; the native-owned report is sealed again before saving. The writer preserves all original indirect objects, unselected tag fields, unknown keys inside the retained single-owner attribute dictionaries, streams, MCIDs, content ownership and page resources, then reopens the candidate and compares intended object fingerprints. Only the selected tag fields and the required root IDTree field may change. Original PDF bytes are retained by the copy workflow.

Cancellation now awaits native job settlement and fails explicitly if termination/cleanup was not observed. Preview discard/destroy operations are tracked and awaited before rebuilding or closing. A cleanup failure retains the departure guard and disables further building/saving rather than announcing successful cancellation. These lifecycle changes have only been source reviewed and syntax checked.

Still unavailable: automatic header inference, creating/moving/splitting/merging existing tree elements across parents, irregular or class/revision/multiple-owner table remediation, namespace/PDF 2.0 authoring, interactive field property changes, link destination edits in this workspace, semantic acceptance, and PDF/UA / Section 508 certification. Existing initial-tagging support and its separate limits are unchanged. This checkpoint supersedes the older statement in PDF-TAG-TREE-PROGRESS.md that header associations require preexisting identifiers/IDTree and that identifiers cannot be authored.

Attribute decisions were checked against the primary [ISO 32000-1:2008 specification hosted by Adobe](https://opensource.adobe.com/dc-acrobat-sdk-docs/standards/pdfstandards/pdf/PDF32000_2008.pdf), clause 14.8.5 and tables 347–349. # F66 thin-line inspection and reviewed repair — October 12, 2026

Implemented a bounded, contained vector stroke inspector and a preserving native repair path. This is a supported slice of F66; the full target stays open.

`PdfThinLineWorkspace` enters from the native PDF reader. The user chooses a physical-point threshold, inspects page/object/content-stream/operator locations, selects individual supported strokes, and chooses a replacement physical minimum. No candidate is selected automatically. Actual original/output pages are rendered side by side; every changed physical page must be viewed and review acknowledged before saving the retained, sealed new copy.

## Evidence and geometry

The lexical scanner is an offset-preserving adaptation of the existing preflight scanner: strings, dictionaries and arrays stay opaque, comments are ignored, operators have checked arity, and nested syntax/token work is bounded. Page Contents arrays form one program so graphics state can span streams. The scanner tracks q/Q, cm, w, ExtGState LW, page UserUnit, invoked Form matrices, path construction, stroke paint operators and conservative path/control-point bounds. Effective widths use CTM singular values, giving directional bounds under anisotropy/shear. Hairlines explicitly have device-dependent physical width. Mid-path transforms and degenerate matrices are uncertain and not repairable.

Limits: 100 MiB input/output, 500 pages, inherited preserving graph traversal (100,000 objects / 300,000 visits), 4 MiB combined program, 32 MiB decoded program work, 1,000,000 lexical tokens, 24 Form levels, 20,000 invocations, 10,000 strokes and 200 selected repairs. The native engine also enforces its global decode allocation/work and containment budgets.

## Preserving repair

Only uniquely referenced, uniquely invoked indirect page-content streams with completely inspected supported programs can be changed. Selected operators receive an explicit replacement `w` immediately before painting and the original width immediately after. Unselected strokes keep their original width, path and matrix. Unchanged program bytes are retained exactly; only selected stream encodings/lengths change. All original objects remain at their original references. Stream lengths are normalized before preservation manifests, matching existing preserving codecs.

The writer snapshots all original object fingerprints, requires every unaffected fingerprint to remain equal, serializes with the native PDF writer, independently reopens, and compares every constructed object fingerprint, trailer, page geometry, stroke path/matrix and selected/unselected widths. Receipts include source/output hashes, source-bound inspection and selection hashes, object manifest hashes and width changes. The service retains source-bound sealed bytes for new-copy save. Renderer PDF.js also independently reopens the actual output, checks changed-page geometry and parses operator lists before review.

Signed, certified, encrypted, permission-constrained, XFA and malformed object graphs are refused by the existing preserving loader/graph policy. Unknown operators, inline images and unsupported graphics-state semantics explicitly report incomplete program coverage and disable repairs for identified strokes in that program.

## Open F66 scope

Invoked Forms are recursively inspected, including inherited resources and matrices, but repairs within Forms remain unavailable. Pattern programs, Type 3 glyph strokes, text stroke rendering, annotation/widget appearances, transparency/reference Forms and uninvoked Forms remain unsupported. Stroke adjustment, clipping/visibility effects and device rendering are not proved. Anisotropic reported minimum/maximum are directional bounds; they are not an assertion that every path segment has that width. Bounding boxes enclose path/control points and exclude stroke expansion; they are location evidence rather than exact ink extents.

This implementation does not establish universal vector repair, complete visual print preflight or commercial editor parity. Root integration owns IPC registration, native operation allowlists, sealed save flow and the single generated-fixture contained write/source-unchanged/independent-reopen focused check. This subtask performs one syntax/model check only; no build or broad sweep is included.

# TIFF CCITT decoder progress

The existing contained TIFF path now decodes fax strips through the new `desktop/tiff-ccitt-codec.cjs` helper. `desktop/tiff-codec.cjs` calls it only for compression tags 2, 3 and 4. Existing grayscale, palette, RGB, PackBits, LZW, Deflate and orientation functionality remains available.

## Implemented fax modes

- Compression 2: Modified Huffman alternating white/black runs, terminating/makeup codewords, extended makeup lengths, initial zero white run, and byte alignment between rows.
- Compression 3: Group 3 1D and mixed 1D/2D rows, EOL markers and line-mode tags, strip-local reference rows and T4Options EOL byte fill. Every mixed strip starts with a 1D row.
- Compression 4: Group 4 2D pass, horizontal and vertical offsets −3 through +3, an initial all-white reference row for every strip, contiguous row codes and a required EOFB marker.
- FillOrder 1 and 2 are applied to compressed input bits. Output is normalized to MSB-first packed bilevel pixels. Existing TIFF photometric handling preserves WhiteIsZero and reverses the decoded white/black meaning for BlackIsZero; the existing orientation transform then produces the RGB page PNG.

Fax input requires one unsigned 1-bit sample, grayscale photometric 0 or 1, and predictor 1. T4Options 0, 1, 4 and 5 are accepted. T6Options must be 0. Uncompressed fax extensions, reserved option bits and reserved 2D extension modes are explicitly refused. Invalid codewords, premature endings, excessive or nonadvancing runs, out-of-range changing elements and extra encoded row data cause errors; the decoder does not repair or guess missing rows.

Group 3 TIFF strips may end after the declared rows with byte padding, a final EOL, a complete six-marker RTC, or a final EOL followed by complete RTC. Mixed endings require RTC tags to indicate 1D. Group 4 strips must contain the full EOFB marker and at most seven zero padding bits. Modified Huffman row padding is ignored as specified, and extra bytes after the final row are refused. These ending rules can reject nonconforming fax TIFFs that other viewers attempt to repair.

## Interface and bounds

The helper exposes `decodeCcittStrip(input, {width, rows, compression, fillOrder, t4Options, t6Options, check})` and returns exactly `ceil(width / 8) * rows` packed bytes. It has no filesystem, network, UI, native driver or path interface. No renderer or parent decoder fallback was added.

Existing service and page report contracts are unchanged. The parent inspection validator accepts tags 2/3/4 only with 1-bit grayscale metadata. The service still returns source/token-bound binary PNG pages and independently validates their dimensions, framing, byte lengths and hashes before retaining them. Source fingerprints, original files, cancellation, observed cleanup and the reviewed image/PDF output workflow stay in place.

The existing 100 MiB input, 8,192 pixels per dimension, 16 million page pixels, 64 million collection pixels, 64 MiB page decompression and 32 MiB PNG output budgets remain. Each fax row permits at most `3 * width + 128` code/mode operations; each run permits at most `ceil(width / 64) + 1` makeup/terminating codewords. Huffman codes are bounded to 13 bits and 2D mode prefixes to seven bits. EOL zero fill is limited to 4,096 bits; Group 3 trailing markers are limited to 256 bits and seven markers. Reference-row lookup uses bounded binary search over at most one changing element per pixel. Deadline/cancel callbacks run each row and every 1,024 consumed bits. A 30-second helper deadline supplements the full TIFF job deadline and native containment limits. Failed decoded output is zeroed before release.

## Verification status

The helper, TIFF codec, validation and service passed `node --check`. Source-only checks confirmed the literal codeword table counts (64 white and 64 black terminating words, 27 white and 27 black makeup words, 13 shared makeup words), binary lengths and prefix-free run tables. No TIFF/parser execution, fixtures, new tests, runtime/UI/native/device/PDF tests or image-fidelity comparisons were performed, per the task constraint. Runtime correctness and compatibility remain unverified. The native bundle must be rebuilt so its existing TIFF operation dispatch includes the helper dependency.

Primary references read during implementation: [TIFF 6.0](https://image-js.github.io/tiff/media/TIFF6.pdf), [ITU-T T.4 (07/1996)](https://www.itu.int/rec/dologin_pub.asp?id=T-REC-T.4-199607-S%21%21PDF-E&lang=e&type=items), [ITU-T T.6 (11/1988)](https://www.itu.int/rec/dologin_pub.asp?id=T-REC-T.6-198811-I%21%21PDF-E&lang=e&type=items), and the normative one-dimensional code tables reproduced in [RFC 804](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc804.txt). Codewords are numeric format data; the decoder implementation is local code rather than an imported fax engine.

# Bounded multipage TIFF decoder progress

The TIFF path now has a real TIFF 6 directory parser and strip decoder in `desktop/tiff-codec.cjs`, parent receipt/framing checks in `desktop/tiff-validation.cjs`, a source-bound contained service in `desktop/tiff-service.cjs`, and a page-selection workspace in `src/tiff-workspace.js` and `.css`. Shared routing, IPC and contained engine dispatch are integrated by the parent workstream.

## Supported subset

- Classic TIFF 6, either endian, multiple linked image directories, orientation 1–8 normalized into page PNG pixels.
- Unsigned grayscale (WhiteIsZero/BlackIsZero) and palette pages with 1, 4 or 8 bits per sample; chunky RGB with 8 bits per channel.
- Uncompressed strips, PackBits, TIFF LZW with the TIFF early code-width transition, and zlib Deflate tags 8/32946. Horizontal predictor 2 is accepted for supported 8-bit LZW/Deflate strips.
- Actual RGB PNG encoding using Node's bundled zlib and PNG chunk CRCs, without a paid engine or newly installed dependency.

BigTIFF, tiles, separate-plane samples, alpha/extra samples, signed/float samples, higher bit depths, fax/CCITT and JPEG compression, CMYK/YCbCr/Lab and other photometric modes are explicitly unsupported. Unsupported directories remain visible with a reason and cannot be selected for output. This is a subset decoder, not a claim of complete TIFF support or visual/color equivalence. Color profiles, physical resolution and metadata are omitted. Output remains image-only without OCR text.

## Containment and bounds

Only fixed `tiff-inspect` and `tiff-page` operations are used. The codec has no filesystem or network access interface and accepts byte arrays with an optional abort signal. The service requires an already retained source ID, TIFF extension, byte array and matching SHA-256 fingerprint; it does not accept renderer file paths. There is no direct decoder fallback in the parent or renderer. The native contained runtime must be rebuilt and verified before these operations can run.

Input is limited to 100 MiB, 100 directories, 1,024 entries per directory, 100,000 values per interpreted tag, 16,384 strips per page, 8,192 pixels per dimension, 16 million decoded pixels per page and 64 million supported pixels across the inventory. Each strip is decompressed into an exact declared row budget, with at most 64 MiB decoded page bytes. PNG output is at most 32 MiB per page. A 30-second codec deadline supplements the native broker's wall-clock/termination limits. Cancellation clears retained inspection and PNG copies, awaits the active job and observed broker cleanup, and throws on an unsafe termination or cleanup failure. The workspace preserves a cancellation failure as a departure guard; the service stays closed.

The parent validates exact inert report keys, source SHA-256, page index, orientation-normalized dimensions, output SHA-256/length and PNG signature, chunk sequence and CRCs before retaining a decoded copy. No PNG decompression occurs in these parent checks. Preview uses only the verified PNG in the renderer. A bounded LRU retains at most ten PNG pages, 100 MiB and 64 million pixels. Selected output must be revalidated against the current source and operation token; cached pages are cleared/zeroed on discard and disposal.

## Integration contract

`new TiffWorkspace(root, file, {announce, beforeImport, onImported, setGuard, services})` exposes `open`, `prepareDeparture`, `releaseDeparture`, and `dispose`. Default services are `window.pdfix`. Required methods are `tiffInspect(id, token)`, `tiffPage(id, token, pageIndex)`, `tiffImport(id, token, pageIndices)`, `tiffCancel(id, token)` and `tiffDiscard(id, token)`.

`TiffService.inspect(id, source, token)` returns `{token, report}`. `page(id, source, token, index)` returns `{token, bytes, report}` with native-binary PNG bytes. `output(id, source, token, indices)` returns `{token, sourceSha256, pages: [{bytes, report}]}` in requested output order. Import should touch/decode each selected page in order immediately before `output`, then save exclusive PNG copies through the existing scanner/image source pipeline, retaining the original TIFF. Import receives one to ten distinct indices and stays within the existing image collection's pixel and byte budgets.

Each page must be previewed and explicitly checked for artwork/orientation before adding it. Selection can be reordered or removed. Import transfers the selected PNG copies into the existing image workspace, whose PDF preview and save review remain necessary. A canceled import retains the TIFF selection. Source-page review is temporary and does not substitute for PDF layout review.

## Verification limits

All new JavaScript files were checked with `node --check`. No runtime decoder execution, TIFF fixtures, newly written tests, UI tests, native/device tests or PDF tests were run, following the task constraint. Decoder correctness, image fidelity, cancellation and end-to-end import remain unverified at runtime. The parent workstream performs the permitted compilation/build checks after routing is integrated.

The implementation was read against the primary [TIFF 6.0 specification](https://image-js.github.io/tiff/media/TIFF6.pdf), including strip organization, orientation, PackBits, LZW and horizontal prediction. [LibTIFF's coverage reference](https://libtiff.gitlab.io/libtiff/specification/coverage.html) helps identify broader TIFF modes that this subset does not claim.

The editable reorder/Bates workspace can save up to 20 named step definitions in the app's user data folder. A definition stores its page count and step settings; loading it into a PDF with a different page count is refused. Saving a definition never creates a PDF. The store is `document-workflow-library.json` under Electron's trusted `userData` folder. It contains definition names, step settings, source hashes for drafts, and timestamps. These settings are **not encrypted**. No PDF bytes, output PDF, arbitrary user-selected file path, native receipt, or review state is stored. The store has a 128 KiB size limit, per-step validation, and atomic replacement; a malformed store is left untouched and reads/writes fail closed. Storage failures are shown in the workspace. Deletion requires pressing the explicit Delete selected workflow or Clear recovery draft control.

Native API contract: `new DocumentWorkflowLibrary(userDataFolder)` exposes `listDefinitions()`, `saveDefinition(name,pageCount,steps)`, `loadDefinition(id,pageCount)`, `removeDefinition(id)`, `saveDraft(sourceSha256,pageCount,steps)`, `readDraft(sourceSha256,pageCount)`, and `clearDraft(sourceSha256)`. The main process must derive the draft source hash and page count from the selected source, never from renderer-supplied values. The renderer bridge names are `listDocumentWorkflowDefinitions`, `saveDocumentWorkflowDefinition`, `loadDocumentWorkflowDefinition`, `removeDocumentWorkflowDefinition`, `saveDocumentWorkflowDraft`, `readDocumentWorkflowDraft`, and `clearDocumentWorkflowDraft`.

# Fixed contained XFDF comment import

Saved 2026-10-04. `PdfXfdfImportService` uses the packaged Windows AppContainer document engine exclusively. Incoming XFDF XML and target PDF decoding, annotation creation and source-preserving output reopening happen in the fixed child. The trusted parent validates inert proposals/receipts and hashes; it never parses the XML or PDF and never opens resource references from the input.

## Main/preload contract

`desktop/pdf-xfdf-import-service.cjs` exports `PdfXfdfImportService`, with optional established `{runtimeDirectory,stagingDirectory}` constructor configuration:

```js
await service.inspect(id,source,{xfdf:canonicalBase64});
await service.build(id,source,token,{
  xfdf:canonicalBase64,
  proposalSha256:reviewedProposalHash,
  keys:explicitDistinctSelectedRowKeys
});
service.output(id,currentSource,token);
await service.cancel(id,token); // token optional for active inspection
await service.discard(id,token);
await service.dispose();
await service.status();
```

Inspection returns the validated source/XML-bound proposal directly. Build returns `{token,bytes,report,receiptSha256}`; the receipt SHA is computed over canonical report JSON followed by a newline. Output returns the sealed native PDF bytes/report for saving. The renderer supplies neither saved output bytes nor a source path. Source ID/SHA, XML SHA, proposal hash, selected-row hash and token/generation remain bound to the exact job. Saved preview bytes and receipts are detached from native-owned immutable output. Current source fingerprint and sealed source/XML/proposal/output hashes are rechecked by output().

Main owns the explicit `.xfdf` picker and bounded read. Its renderer response is `{name,bytes:Uint8Array,sha256}`; read at most 8 MiB from a regular chosen file, detect growth/short reads and never accept renderer paths/URLs. The renderer converts the selected bytes to canonical base64 for the explicit inspect/build request. The service accepts only the exact `{xfdf}` inspection or `{xfdf,proposalSha256,keys}` draft shape validated by the import codec's pure module. Input XML is at most 8 MiB decoded and cannot substitute another target PDF through XFDF IDs or file/appearance references.

Main/preload routes: `inspectPdfXfdfImport(id,inspection)`, `buildPdfXfdfImport(id,token,draft)`, `cancelPdfXfdfImport(id,token?)`, `discardPdfXfdfImport(id,token)` and `savePdfXfdfImport(id,token)`. Save should use the existing reviewed-PDF exclusive source-bound helper with an imported-comments filename suffix. Root owns those route/status/lifecycle hooks. Await disposal before replacement after renderer loss; retain failed closed service on unsafe rejection and catch disposal errors at quit.

## Fixed engine and bounds

The fixed operations are `xfdf-import-inspect` and `xfdf-import-build`. Inspection options carry canonical base64 only; build carries the validated exact draft. No command, executable, path, URL, dynamic import or alternate worker is selectable.

Accepted XML remains at most 8 MiB, 1,000 source annotations, 200 selected creations, 200,000 aggregate coordinate values and 8 MiB proposal/receipt. Proposal and result validators bound exact inert geometry/style/literal metadata, source/page identities, supported types, notes, new annotation/AP references and the reopened output inventory. Parent additionally checks original source byte length and XML SHA against its owned input. The existing PDF source/copy limit is 100 MiB; signed/encrypted/certified/unsupported source refusals remain in the preserving writer.

Canonical base64 expands an 8 MiB XML file beyond the ordinary 2 MiB request cap. These two operations therefore receive a **12 MiB request.json** budget, enough for the accepted XML plus source/proposal/selection envelope. **Every earlier operation retains its 2 MiB parent and child request cap.** The broker's fixed read-only request slot is bounded to 12 MiB and its aggregate staging watchdog to 244 MiB plus marker/error overhead. Output JSON remains globally 32 MiB with the stricter 8 MiB import domain receipts; import parent traversals cap at 750,000 inert nodes/depth100 so accepted ink/quad coordinate scope does not exceed the generic 300,000-node cap. This is a bounded watchdog, not an OS disk quota.

All launches still verify the pinned broker/runtime bytes and exact AppContainer/job token policy. Shared two-job process leases, one-job family slots, observed broker close, cleanup-before-release and permanent unsafe-failure closure are reused. The status-only package cache remains independent of every launch check. The qpdf mode, handles, capabilities, file ACL grants and Node/Job Object memory/process/deadline limits are unchanged.

## Scope and verification

The document/PDF-editing agent owns the XFDF parser, appearance adapter, preserving codec, schema validators and reviewed UI. This service does not broaden their supported annotation mapping, create certificate trust, execute scripts/resources or silently overwrite existing annotations. Revu/private appearances, full XFDF conformance and runtime viewer acceptance remain open.

## S00 — Security Sandbox (explicit user addition)

Required: Windows OS containment for native document engines; job-only file grants; no network capability; bounded memory/processes/time; cancellation kills the contained process; no unsandboxed fallback. Renderer sandbox, blocked active document content, narrow IPC and chosen-file grants remain mandatory. Native Node workers are not OS sandboxes. Security review and hidden runtime containment checks remain release gates.

references.text: - [ ] **A14 — Isolated form-logic compatibility.** Inventory form calculations, validation, formatting and button actions. Prefer narrowly supported declarative calculations; evaluate a dedicated contained compatibility runtime only for required features. Document-origin code must have no ambient file, process or network access, with resource bounds and effective isolation proof. General PDF script/macro execution remains disabled in current and first-release readers. Later compatibility is explicitly gated on a separate reviewed design and does not relax S00 or R08.

- [ ] **A17 — PDF portfolio navigation and creation.** Add an inert inventory, searchable grid/list navigation, supported previews, extraction and creation/reordering of selected contents. Preserve names/metadata where supported and report unsupported layouts. Apply attachment size/count/decompression limits, traversal protection and contained decoders. Embedded Office, CAD or media content needs its own supported capability; never auto-run extracted files. Interactive 3D portfolio presentation is a separate renderer evaluation within this target. (M10.02; S00/R08.)

- [ ] **A20 — Embedded multimedia.** Evaluate user-initiated audio/video playback with inert inventory, codec support, licensing, bounded decode and cancellation. No automatic playback, remote retrieval or script/plugin execution. Rich-media actions require separately reviewed supported behavior. (M10.02; S00.)

- [ ] **A25 — Robust opening, repair and honest failure.** Make F42's corpus explicit for legacy/PostScript-derived, malformed, truncated, mixed-generator, unusual-font/image, encrypted, giant and adversarial PDFs. Add bounded cancellable diagnostics, useful error causes and reviewed repair-to-copy where supported. Measure opening/navigation/selection/memory responsiveness across hardware profiles and verify repairs preserve supported content. Never silently call a partially rendered document complete or raise limits without resource evidence. (R06–R09/R29; F04/F29/F42; S00.)

references.text: - [ ] **A06 — Color-profile conversion.** Review ICC profiles, device-independent color, RGB/CMYK/spot-color handling and explicit output intents. Preview changes, disclose color loss, preserve supported objects and validate conversions against a print corpus. Engine/profile licensing and distribution are prerequisites. (F40; expands M10.02's first-release boundary.)

- [ ] **A17 — PDF portfolio navigation and creation.** Add an inert inventory, searchable grid/list navigation, supported previews, extraction and creation/reordering of selected contents. Preserve names/metadata where supported and report unsupported layouts. Apply attachment size/count/decompression limits, traversal protection and contained decoders. Embedded Office, CAD or media content needs its own supported capability; never auto-run extracted files. Interactive 3D portfolio presentation is a separate renderer evaluation within this target. (M10.02; S00/R08.)

- [ ] **A18 — Interactive 3D PDF.** Evaluate U3D/PRC decoding, rotation, assembly visibility, cross-sections and calibrated geometry measurements with explicit units. Review licensing, GPU/resource budgets and containment. Embedded model viewing and measuring do not imply CAD authoring. (M10.02; separate from M03.12.)

- [ ] **A19 — Geospatial PDF.** Inspect coordinate reference systems, georegistration, latitude/longitude and map measurements. Show unit/projection/precision and calibration limits, support layers where meaningful and verify against known reference maps. Local PDF measurements do not establish accurate GIS coordinates. (M10.02.)

- [ ] **A20 — Embedded multimedia.** Evaluate user-initiated audio/video playback with inert inventory, codec support, licensing, bounded decode and cancellation. No automatic playback, remote retrieval or script/plugin execution. Rich-media actions require separately reviewed supported behavior. (M10.02; S00.)

Report that revocation controls supported clients and cannot recall screenshots or unrestricted copies. Show service destination, identity and retention. Adobe/AEM policy-file interoperability requires supported API/licensing evaluation; never bypass another system's DRM. Password encryption is a separate existing feature. (M10.02; service/security evaluation.)

The top bar has **Collapse sidebar**, **Focus mode** and **Enter fullscreen**. Use **F11** for native fullscreen, **Ctrl Shift B** for the sidebar and **Ctrl Shift F** for focus mode. **Esc** closes a dialog first, then exits fullscreen or focus mode. Sidebar and PDF pane choices are remembered locally. **View options → Pages panel/Search panel** toggles reader panes; search is closed until needed; **Find in PDF** or **Ctrl F** reopens PDF search. **Fit page** shows the whole page; **Rotate view** changes only the displayed orientation. **Pages/Outline/Saved** navigate thumbnails, embedded document bookmarks or personal saved pages. **Save page** (Ctrl D) stores a named page locally; the last-read page is remembered. These positions/bookmarks are bound to the source bytes and are cleared with recent-file metadata. Print and Save a copy preserve the original page orientation. Reading-text view temporarily becomes artwork. Escape/F11 and a temporary auto-hiding exit button restore the previous view and the prior native fullscreen state. Entry/exit/reader cleanup serialize; external native fullscreen exit is handled. Modal dialogs must finish first. Documents, comments, recovery drafts and ledger data are not exported or rewritten by this view change.
